Entry: sprint template step 2 (F/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md, 'Where it refuses, stop: this file may be a draft the owner never approved, or the review estate lacks the .ok-planner/review/config.json the command reads') -> 'stop it as step 11 says' -> step 11 writes <sprint-name>-stopped.txt and runs '.ok-planner/bin/review certified --sprint <path>'. Where the path ends: review:main calls project_root() and load_config(root) before args.run, so with .ok-planner/review/ or its config.json missing (or a config lacking block_sources/standards/python/prompts_dir) review certified exits 1 with 'review: cannot read .ok-planner/review/config.json: ...' (or 'no .ok-planner/review directory ...' / 'declares no ...') before cmd_certified ever reaches stop_reason. No SPRINT STOPPED line is printed, so the goal rule ('The goal also ends, unmet, when that command prints SPRINT STOPPED') never fires and a /goal checker keeps pushing the stopped session -- the exact harm decision:every-stop-ends-the-goal ('a stop before the run files its first task') and WI 7 bullet 2-3 name. The same holds where step 12 stops because sprint certification is unrunnable for the same missing review config. Scope: caused by the change (the stop-record path and its reliance on review certified are new in this sprint; at base 8ada3ba the template only said 'name its message to the owner and stop').

body: Entry A3 (an operator's script gives an error that does not say what they did wrong, and later use keeps failing). Trigger: two scenarios X and Y whose tests live in one test file F; the write stage filed test task tX (files [F]) and then tY (files [F], after [tX], from holders_of/planned_file); both closed blocked having filed support items (or tY closed partial or was running), and the run stopped before the next --stage write. On resume, sprint step 3 runs tasks retry --all, which reopens tX and tY (open, issued=0), then step 4 runs tests tasks --stage write. Path: tests:stage_write -> holders_of (holders[F] = tY, the later open holder) -> blocked_on_support matches tX through reopened_on_support (tests:3968) -> the reopened branch adds the holders of tX's own files to its waits, tests:4133 'waits |= {holders[path] for path in task.get("files") or [] if path in holders}', so waits = {the support task, tY}; waits.discard only drops tX itself -> planned_after (tests:4138) -> filed_tasks 'after' op -> set_task_list (tests:3752) -> tasks task set tX --field after=[..., tY] -> tasks::cmd_task -> check_dependencies fails 'task tX would wait on itself through ...' because tY waits on tX. Harm: --stage write raises 'tasks task set ... failed: task tX would wait on itself' after it already filed the support tasks earlier in the filings list; every later --stage write computes the same waits and fails the same way, so the resumed run can never get past the write stage and stops again as a genuine blocker. For an open task, the latest holder of its own file is either itself or a task chained after it, so adding holders of its own files always closes a loop; at base the branch ran only for closed-blocked tasks, which holders_of skips, so their holders were tasks to wait on. The same loop arises with a legacy task holding F filed after tX. Scope: caused by the change (the reopened branch and the after op are new in this sprint, notes item 7 'Notes review: on resume, --stage write treats a reopened, unissued test task ...').

Entry A8, design commitment decision:test-support-written-before-tests ('a test task that finds its support short records what it needs ... and writes no test; a support task makes the change before the test task runs again'), which the sprint's notes (item 7, Notes review) apply to a reopened test task. Trigger: on resume, a reopened test task T (open, unissued) filed an open support item I at path P, and P is held by an open support task S1 (S1 reopened by retry --all, or released from running), so tests:stage_support leaves I unbriefed (P in 'held') and files no support task for it. Path: tests:stage_write blocked loop -> the skip 'if closed_blocked(task) and any(... not in briefed ...)' does not apply to a reopened task -> waits = {latest_support[P]} = {S1} (tests:4132) -> planned_after(T, {S1}). Harm: when S1 closes, tasks close's step issues T, and T runs again before any support task has made I (the support task that briefs I is only filed by the next --stage write, after the drain), so the test task meets the same shortfall a second time, the reverse of the order the decision commits to. At base a closed-blocked task in this case was deferred until I was briefed and then refiled after the support task that briefs it. Scope: caused by the change (the reopened branch is new in this sprint).

tests::stage_write. Before: the write stage read no testing setting; under testing.enabled off with a -plan.json standing, or with a testing missing a key testing_config requires, it filed support, test, and legacy tasks. After: it calls testing_config(root, sprint) after the preflight branch and before any filing, and refuses with testing_config's message (off: 'sets testing.enabled to off, so no sprint plans or runs tests: run /ok-setup ...'; a missing key: names the keys and says to declare them), filing nothing. Users: (1) sprint-document.md steps 2 and 4, which open the test stages where -plan.json stands or testing.enabled is on: under off, at base the filed test tasks could not edit a test path (the lint's no-tests check allows test edits only under on or frozen) and could not run tests run --sprint, which already refused under off, so the stage could not reach its goal; now it refuses plainly and step 4's refusal is a genuine blocker under step 11 with an actionable message. Under on or frozen with a full testing config nothing changes. (2) converge SKILL step 5a, which runs --stage write only where the testing state is not off, after a whole-suite round whose tests run --sprint already ran testing_config; no new refusal is reachable there. (3) cmd_tasks passes the refusal through as InputError like every other stage refusal. A missing key is the operator's configuration grossly wrong, which the accept list leaves standing. No user across a boundary: tests tasks is internal to the suite and ships with its callers.

body: WI 7 resume facet, notes call 'On resume, --stage write treats a reopened, unissued test task that has an open support item as blocked on support, and adds the support task it files to that test task's after' (decision test-support-written-before-tests: 'a support task makes the change before the test task runs again'). Entry: sprint step 3 'tasks retry --all' -> step 4 'tests tasks --stage write' -> tests:stage_write -> stage_support -> blocked_on_support -> planned_after -> filed_tasks. Where it ends: stage_support puts an open item in open_items only when 'path not in held' (tests:4005); where another open support task S0 (one that does not cite the item, e.g. a support task reopened by retry --all, or one filed for another scenario) holds the item's path, no support task is filed for the item. stage_write's loop then skips the item only for a closed-blocked task ('if closed_blocked(task) and any(... not in briefed)', tests:4128); for the reopened task it goes on and planned_after adds only latest_support[path] = S0 (tests:4132-4138). When S0 closes, cmd_close's step issues the test task, which runs before any support task makes its item; the next --stage write no longer sees it (reopened_on_support needs 'not task.get("issued")'). Second trigger: an open item with no path (support_item_path empty) gives empty waits, and 'elif waits:' adds nothing, so the first 'next' of step 7's drain issues the task at once. Outcome not reached: the reopened test task runs before the support it recorded exists. Scope: caused by the change (reopened_on_support, planned_after, and the closed_blocked guard are new).

Entry A1 (a second writer between two steps of one change). Trigger: build B2 waits on B1 (step 4 chains stages whose files overlap). B1 closes partial; cmd_close's step issues B2 (ready() counts any close); B2 runs and closes blocked. The session refiles B1 as R1 (B2 is closed, so cmd_refile does not append R1 to B2's after). The run then stops with R1 not done and B2 not yet refiled. Path on resume: sprint step 3 'tasks retry --all' -> tasks:cmd_retry -> retry_kind (B2: closed blocked, no task names it previous -> retried; R1 -> retried or released) -> retry_records -> reset_task, which keeps B2's after ['B1'] as the notes rule ('A reopened task keeps its brief, files, and after list'). B1 stays closed (refiles_of names it), so ready(B2) holds at once, and the drain's next issues B2 and R1 together: two agents edit the overlapping files at once, and B2 builds before B1's remainder lands. retry_records un-issues only waiters whose after names a reopened task (tasks:1262-1266); it never follows a reopened task's own after to the latest refile, as tests:latest_of does for the test stages. Quote, tasks:1263: 'named = sorted(reopened & set(t.get("after") or []))'. Scope: caused by the change (retry --all, WI 7, reopens such a task on every resume).

Entry A1. cmd_refile promises (USAGE) that 'every open task that waited on the task waits on the refile too', but it only appends the refile's id to each open waiter's after (tasks:1049-1050) and leaves its issued=1 as it stands. A waiter's issued was set when the source closed (cmd_close -> step -> ready() counts any close, tasks:786-791), and cmd_claim checks issued alone (tasks:1106), so the waiter stays claimable before the refile runs. Trigger on WI 3's own path: sprint step 7 refiles a build B1 that closed partial ('tasks refile <task> --files <its files and that path>'); B2, chained after B1 because their files overlap, was issued when B1 closed and is claimed beside the refile: two writers on one file. Also: the refile copies the source's after as it stands (tasks:1035), not each dependency's latest refile, so refiling a blocked B2 whose after names a refiled B1 waits on the closed B1, not its open refile. I1 fixed the issued-waiter half of this class in cmd_retry only (retry_records un-issues waiters). Scope: stood at base; reached by the change (WI 3 changed cmd_refile and step 7 now routes through it).

Entry A9 (a message tells a user something not so). I2's refusal fires for every refiled task retry_kind rejects: 'if kind is None and t["id"] in refiled: fail("task %s was refiled as %s; retry %s" ...)' (tasks:1295-1296). refiles_of maps a task to its immediate refile only. Triggers: (1) /converge refiles a root that closed done (SKILL.md: 'tasks retry refuses a done close'); 'tasks retry <that root>' now answers 'retry tM' though tM is open or running and 'retry tM' refuses; (2) in a chain T -> R -> R2, 'retry T' names R, which itself is refused and names R2. Before the change a done task got the accurate 'neither running ... nor closed as one of ...'. The operator follows the advice and gets a second refusal. Scope: caused by the change (I2).

body: WI 6 outcome not reached for a commit that bears on a docspec through its claim ledger. Entry: docs start (cmd_start) and the stamp guard (cmd_stamp -> later_commits_bearing) both decide 'bears on' through bearing_docspecs, which unions change_reasons alone: docspec file, corpus/code references, declaring files, Where paths. docs window (window_entry) also reaches a docspec on its stale claims: entry['status'] = 'reached' if reasons or stale, stale = stale_claims(state, changed), where a claim is stale when any file in its 'sources' changed (core.md:401: sources names each file the claim rests on, any file, not only the docspec's References). Trigger: after /plan-docs records the plan's commit, the owner commits a change to a file that a ledger claim of a planned docspec names in its sources and that no References/Where/declaring entry matches. docs start: bearing_docspecs returns {} -> 'start: no commit ... bears on' exit 0, the run starts. The plan's 'Claims to check again' list was taken before the commit, so no checker rechecks that claim. cmd_stamp: stale = claims stale between old_stamp and base -> the claim is dropped from the ledger (ledger_after excludes stale_ids) while its text stays in the document unchecked; slug not in later['bearing'] -> state['stamp'] = args.commit. Next docs window diffs from the archive commit, so the docspec stands 'current' (no reasons, no stale claims) though the commit after the plan made a documented claim stale: the work item's 'docs window never reports such a docspec current' fails. Same failure on a resumed run for an owner commit after the base: stale_ids are computed old_stamp..base (cmd_stamp 'between' diff), so a claim whose source changed after the base is kept as held and stamped over. Scope: caused (bearing_docspecs, cmd_start, later_commits_bearing are new in this change).

WI 6 outcome defeated by the handoff's rewrite. The new handoff text: 'For a documentation sprint, once the commits are made, write the output of git rev-parse HEAD into its Window's Planned against commit line in place of the commit the plan recorded: those commits hold only what the plan already read from the tree'. The rewrite moves the planned commit to HEAD without checking that every commit between the recorded commit and HEAD is one the handoff itself just made from paths the window read. Trigger: /plan-docs step 2 records HEAD and runs docs window; during the interactive session (planners, worked-example and unexplained-change questions, approval) the owner commits product work in another terminal, or edits a file after the window ran that the handoff then groups and commits. The handoff makes its commits and writes HEAD into the Window line. docs start then sees HEAD == planned -> 'start: ... no commit follows the plan', exit 0; cmd_stamp's later_commits_bearing measures from the rewritten commit, so every planned docspec is stamped at the archive commit and the next docs window starts after the commit the plan never read: the docspec it bears on is reported current, which WI 6 forbids ('A product commit made between the plan's commit and the run's start stays in the next /plan-docs window for every docspec it bears on'). Before the change the plan line was never rewritten. Scope: caused (the rewrite sentence is new in this change).

A9 on a path the change added: docs start reports that the plan does not cover commits the plan did read. Path: shared.md {{PLANNING-HANDOFF}} -> the owner answers no to the proposed commits (or some paths still stand after the commits: 'go on as on a no'); the handoff names the paths and says 'execution's base step refuses to start while any such path stands uncommitted', and hands over no goal line, and the Window line is not rewritten (the rewrite runs only 'once the commits are made'). The owner then commits those same paths by hand, as the message directs, and runs /goal. doc-sprint-document.md step 3 -> docs start -> cmd_start -> bearing_docspecs(planned, HEAD): the owner's commits change the files the window reached the docspec on (that is why it was planned), so it prints 'start stopped: commits between the planned commit ... bear on these docspecs' and 'The plan does not cover these commits, so the plan must be made again with /plan-docs before the run files a task.' (scripts/docs cmd_start), exit 2. Step 3 writes the stop record 'docs start: the plan must be made again', and plan-docs SKILL.md section 1 then offers to set the plan aside and offers no /goal. Harm: the message is false: docs window reads the working tree (changed_since diffs the stamp against the tree plus untracked files), so the plan read exactly those changes; the owner acts on it by discarding an approved, valid plan and planning again. Before the change, the same owner commit followed by /goal recorded the base and ran. Scope: caused (docs start and the step 3 stop are new).

WI 7 ('The session files no stage twice'; notes: 'file no task whose role and key the run already holds') not reached on a resumed documentation sprint. Step 5 says: 'On a resumed run, here and in steps 6 and 7, file no task whose role and key the run already holds, as tasks status lists them.' tasks status (scripts/tasks cmd_status) prints only open tasks ('for t in open_tasks: print("open ...")', open_tasks = state != closed) plus the ids of closed retryable tasks; a task that closed done is never listed, in text or --json. Path: step 4 on resume -> tasks use -> tasks retry --all reopens every task that did not close done -> step 5 reads tasks status, which lists those reopened tasks and none of the done ones -> every write item whose writer task already closed done is absent from the listing, so the session files a second writer task with the same role and key (tasks file refuses no duplicate key); steps 6 and 7 likewise refile done style and checker tasks. The writer reruns on a document already written and checked, and its claims are recorded again. Step 7's 'the loop goes on from the highest round the run records' has the same gap: the round lives in closed checker task keys (<slug>:<round>:<n>), which tasks status does not show (its 'round:' line is the tracker's own round, which this run never sets). Scope: caused (the resume rule is new).

WI 7 ('every stop must end the goal') not reached on one pre-run stop step 3 names. Step 3: 'First check .ok-planner/bin/tasks, .ok-planner/bin/docs, and the profile ok-opus ...: a missing one is the front door's administration (/ok) to materialize, so stop and say so', and every stop goes 'as {{CEREMONY-RUN-RULES}} says': write the stop record, then 'run .ok-planner/bin/docs complete --sprint <path>, show its output whole, and stop'. Where the missing tool is .ok-planner/bin/docs itself, that command cannot run, so no DOCS STOPPED line ever appears in the session. Step 1's stop condition, stated to /goal's checker, which reads only the session, ends the goal only on DOCS COMPLETE or DOCS STOPPED printed by that command; the goal rule says the same. So on this stop the checker sees neither line and the goal keeps looping, the exact harm WI 7 names ('runs have stopped while the goal kept looping and spending tokens'). The builder recorded this as divergence call i24 and left it. The sprint template has the same gap for a missing .ok-planner/bin/review (outside this pass's area; noted for the merge agent). Scope: caused (the stop-record mechanism and its goal line are new).

body: Work item 6 (a product commit made between the plan's commit and the run's start stays in the next window; docs window never reports such a docspec current) is reached only in part. Entry point: /plan-docs step 2 (SKILL.md:26) records git rev-parse HEAD as the Window's 'Planned against commit' and computes the window then; the planners read the tree after it. The handoff (shared.md, PLANNING-HANDOFF, the paragraph after the commits) then overwrites that line with git rev-parse HEAD after its commits, on the claim that 'those commits hold only what the plan already read from the tree'. That claim does not hold: (a) any commit the owner made out of band between step 2 and the handoff is now an ancestor of the rewritten line, and (b) the handoff commits every path git status lists outside .ok-planner/ at handoff time, including an edit made after step 2's window. Trigger: the owner commits a change to a file a planned docspec references (or edits it uncommitted, which the handoff then commits) while the /plan-docs session runs past step 2, and the handoff makes a commit. Path: handoff rewrites Window to HEAD -> doc-sprint step 3 docs:cmd_start sees planned == HEAD and prints 'start: ... no commit follows the plan', exit 0 -> base = HEAD -> docs:cmd_stamp later_commits_bearing finds planned == parent of the archive commit, returns no bearing -> every planned docspec stamped at the archive commit -> the next docs window diffs from that stamp and never sees the change, so the docspec can stand current. Outcome: the commit the work item names is stamped over. Scope: caused by the change (the rewrite is new in this sprint, from the notes review of work item 6).

Rule: decision documentation-claim-ledger, 'the ledger never holds a claim no checker confirmed at its stamp' (and the USAGE text 'Every claim in the ledger held at the stamp'). cmd_stamp computes the stale set of kept ledger claims from git diff old_stamp..base (docs:cmd_stamp, 'between = git(root, "diff", ..., old_stamp, base, "--")'), then, for a docspec not in later['bearing'], stamps it at args.commit. A commit landing between the base and the parent of --commit is never counted against kept claims. later_commits_bearing only moves the stamp back for a docspec the window reasons (change_reasons: docspec, corpus/code references, declaring files, documentation paths) bear on; a claim's own 'sources' can name a file outside those, which stale_claims checks but change_reasons does not. Trigger: a documentation sprint stops midway (step 8 / CEREMONY-RUN-RULES), the owner commits a change to a file a kept ledger claim lists in its sources but that the docspec's References do not cover, and a new /goal resumes; docs start passes (no window reason fires), the base is kept (B27 resume), and the claim's file is not rewritten. Path: doc-sprint step 3 keeps base -> run completes -> archive commit X -> docs:cmd_stamp: stale over old_stamp..base misses the commit -> ledger_after keeps the claim -> state['stamp'] = X. Harm: the ledger holds, stamped at X, a claim no checker confirmed after its source changed, and the next docs window diffs from X and never marks it stale. Scope: the code stood at the base, and the change reaches it: resume keeping the base (B27, work item 7) is new in this sprint and is the step that puts owner commits between the base and the archive commit, and work item 6 changed cmd_stamp to read commits up to the parent of --commit for the stamp alone, not for the ledger.

body: B26 (and B24's test-tools half) ruling: 'migrate: true-up rewrites the boilerplate from retired-boilerplate.json ... with no code change'. What an old user gets: current_section (true-up:2147) replaces a non-equal hunk only where the live sprint's old lines hold a retired line ('if equal or not held: out.extend(old); continue'). A hunk that is a pure insertion in the carried template (old = []) holds no retired line, so its carried lines are never written. Simulated current_boilerplate (the functions copied verbatim, run on scratch copies) over this repo's own live sprint, laid out by v30.2.0, and over the v30.2.0 and v29.0.0 template blocks: the Completion contract comes out current, but How to execute keeps four gaps: step 4 loses 'On a resumed run, file no stage twice. File no build task for a work item some build task's --cites already names ...'; step 6 loses 'On a resumed run, build the checklist from the run ...'; and the test-stage text a124cfa added (step 3 'Where step 2 found that the run opens its test stages, open them: ...' with its prompt registrations and pool config, step 4's whole '--stage write/verify/sweep/speed' paragraph, step 7's test-stage refile and refusal paragraph, step 10's calls-pool sentence) never lands. Trigger: an owner trues up a project holding a sprint an earlier release planned that stopped mid-run, then starts /goal. Old outcome (base): no resume at all. New outcome: step 3 now runs 'tasks use' and 'tasks retry --all', then step 4, lacking the resume rule, files one build task per stage again, so two build tasks of one stage write the same files; and step 2 now says the run 'opens its test stages (step 3)' while step 3 carries no test-stage opening. The doc-sprint kind simulates clean (v30.2.0, v29.0.0). Scope: current_section stood at base; the change reaches it, because the sprint's B24/B26 migration relies on it and its new step 4 and step 6 lines are pure insertions; the a124cfa half stood at base, unreleased, and ships in the same release.

A3. Trigger: a project whose git repository uses SHA-256 object names (git init --object-format=sha256; the sprint's own review::default_base call names such repositories as supported). Path: /plan-docs records 'git rev-parse HEAD' (plan-docs/SKILL.md:26) into the Window's 'Planned against commit `<sha>`.' line, and {{PLANNING-HANDOFF}} (skills/_sprint/shared.md, new text) rewrites that line to 'git rev-parse HEAD' after its commits; both write a 64-hex name. Documentation sprint step 3 then runs docs::cmd_start -> held_planned_commit -> planned_commit, whose pattern is PLANNED_COMMIT = re.compile(r"^Planned against commit `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`\.$") (scripts/docs:100). It matches no 64-hex line, so cmd_start raises '<sprint> holds no "Planned against commit `<sha>`." line under ## Window; plan the documentation sprint again with /plan-docs', exit 1, and step 3 stops the run with 'docs start: the plan must be made again'. Harm: the plan does hold the line, so the message is false. Planning again writes the same 64-hex line, so no documentation sprint can start in such a repository. Base: docs had no start check and read no planned commit, so a doc sprint ran. Scope: caused by the change (work item 6).

B4 (rewrite): {{TEST-WASTE-RULE}} now names seed data as a waste only 'where the project has a seed `testing.setup` builds'. Users: the B4 notes name tests.md among the planning prompts. tests.md carries the rule in {{TEST-PLANNER-REVIEW-PROMPT}} (tests.md:53) and {{TEST-PLAN-WIDE-REVIEW-PROMPT}} (tests.md:162). Neither prompt's Read list (tests.md:60-84 and 170-190) reads `testing.setup` or .ok-planner/config.json. The sprint did update the other users: tests-story.md:83 and tests-runtime.md:52 read testing.setup, and test-speed.md got a new Read step 5 for it. Goal and source: decision:seed-recommended-never-required and work item 1 say that, where the project has no seed, no reader names a seed and no test-stage prompt or rule names one. What the reviewers get now is a condition they have no input to evaluate. In a seedless project, a planner reviewer or the plan-wide reviewer can still send a scenario back with 'data the test only reads that the seed could hold', which reopens the seed suggestion the owner ruled out. Scope: caused; the rewrite left these two users behind.

body: Artifact: decision every-stop-ends-the-goal, named by work item 7: "Every stop the executor makes before a sprint's contract holds ends the goal: a stop before the run files its first task ... At each, the session writes a stop record beside the sprint that names the reason, then runs review certified, which, while the record stands, prints SPRINT STOPPED". Code site: the sprint template's step 2 (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md) names a pre-run stop where review approved refuses because 'the review estate lacks the .ok-planner/review/config.json the command reads', and stops it 'as step 11 says': write -stopped.txt, then run review certified. But review main (scripts/review:2333-2339) runs load_config(root) and run_under_project_python(root, config) before args.run, and load_config raises ReviewError ('cannot read .ok-planner/review/config.json' or 'declares no <key>', review:152-163) before cmd_certified reaches its stop check (review:2118-2120). What the code does instead: review certified prints 'review: cannot read ...' and exits 1, never SPRINT STOPPED, so a /goal checker that reads only the session sees neither SPRINT COMPLETE nor SPRINT STOPPED and keeps pushing a stopped run, the harm work item 7 was cut to end. Same class, same site shape: step 2's tracker check stops on a missing .ok-planner/bin/tasks, and review loads tasks at import (review:28 load_sibling('issues'), issues:31 load_sibling('tasks')), so review certified cannot start there either; build call i24 records the sibling members for a missing bin/review and bin/docs. In the first ledger I also closed a driver 'blocked' and got the same verdict. The story promises: 'done' means the same thing for every sprint; the completion contract item 3 says 'Where the project has a story, the run's drive ran', and team-execution-cold-gate says drivers try every story and the root forks one pass task per pass. Saw: certified counts filed driver tasks as a drive that ran, though no driver was ever claimed or every driver closed blocked, and counts a review root closed done as 'the find loop ran' though it forked no pass; by contrast an open review root is refused ('holds no review task closed done, so the find loop did not run'). Evidence: 'open t2 task drive key=gate state=open issued=0' / 'open t3 task drive key=gate state=open issued=0' then 'item 3 (certification): holds: the return block names .ok-planner/review/runs/converge-2026-11-08T102000.jsonl, the find loop ran, every defect is settled, 0 stuck defects are listed, and the drive ran over 2 stories' / 'SPRINT COMPLETE: .ok-planner/sprints/certify-completion-drive.md' exit 0; and with review drive-stack printing 'unfilled' (no stack-start and no '- No stack:' line), the same ledger still gave 'the drive ran over 1 stories' and SPRINT COMPLETE, where the contract says 'drive commands unfilled or refused ... mean it did not'.

body: Reviewed /plan-docs and drove its documentation sprint's steps against a scratch project (true-up of the working tree, one docspec 'usage' whose Where is docs/usage.md, a plan with one 'check' item). Followed steps 4-8 of the template exactly: checker t1 recorded one held and one false claim in docs/usage.md; per step 7 a fix writer t2 edited docs/usage.md and set the claim open; checker t3 held the rewrite and set the old claim replaced; step 8 wrote the report and ran docs complete. The story promises: a way to bring every document up to date whenever the owner chooses, so a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands, with the run going unattended to completion (decision documentation-sprints-write-the-documentation: 'the plan runs unattended to completion'). Saw: the template's own steps end in a state its own contract refuses. Step 6 runs the style pass before the fact loop and keeps it 'to the files the `write` and `change` items name', while step 7 files a fix writer 'per file holding a false claim', a `check` item's file included, and completion contract item 1 requires 'every file the run changed that still exists has a style task, except the file of a drop item'. No step files a style task for a check file a fixer changed, so the run can only finish by improvising a style task after the fact loop, whose revision then no checker reads (decision documentation-style-read-once: the style read comes 'After the writers finish'; documentation-claims-checked-until-they-hold: every claim checked until it holds). evidence: '.ok-planner/bin/docs complete --sprint .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-08-usage.md' printed 'DOCS NOT COMPLETE: .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-08-usage.md / - docspec:usage: `docs/usage.md` changed in this run and has no style task', exit 2; after a hand-filed style task t4 it printed 'DOCS COMPLETE', exit 0 (scripts/docs complete_failures: 'if kind != "drop" and path in changed and exists and key not in keys["style"]').

In the scratch project, planned a documentation sprint at HEAD, then committed a product change to tool.sh, a reference of docspec usage. 'docs start --sprint .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-09-usage.md' printed 'start stopped: commits between the planned commit ... and HEAD bear on these docspecs ... The plan does not cover these commits, so the plan must be made again with /plan-docs', exit 2. Wrote the stop record the template's step 3 names, first line 'docs start: the plan must be made again', and ran docs complete. The story promises the owner a way to bring the documentation current whenever they choose; SKILL.md step 1 says of exactly this stop 'the plan can never run: offer to set it aside and plan again, and offer no `/goal`'. Saw: the DOCS STOPPED verdict tells the owner the opposite, so an owner who follows it starts a goal that deletes the record, fails docs start again, and stops with the same reason. evidence: 'DOCS STOPPED: .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-09-usage.md / - docs start: the plan must be made again / ... The run stopped at .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-09-usage-stopped.txt. This ends the goal for this documentation sprint; the owner takes up the reason, and a new /goal resumes the run.', exit 3 (scripts/docs stopped_verdict prints 'and a new /goal resumes the run' for every reason).

body: Reviewed /plan-docs source: SKILL.md, core.md (DOC-PLANNER/WRITE/CHECK prompts), doc-sprint-document.md, and ran scripts/docs window in a scratch project (a new verb in the declaring file and a dropped exception each put the reference docspec in the window: 'declaring file changed: `cli/commands.py`', 'surface intent changed'). Divergence: the fact loop's second listing of a class's members cannot check every file. doc-sprint-document.md step 7 reads: 'File checker tasks of up to six files each, files of one docspec together' and 'The first checker task of a docspec in round 1 also lists the classes its `## Lists` names'; core.md DOC-CHECK-PROMPT has that checker 'Read the docspec ... and each file whole' (the files its brief names) and record 'each public element the documentation omits' as 'missing: <element>'. A reference docspec's layout is 'One file per class the docspec lists' (docs/shapes/reference.md), so a docspec that lists seven or more classes, or one whose reached items name only some of its files, has class files outside that one checker's brief: no checker reads them against the class listing, and the checker cannot tell whether they omit an element. The story promises: reference documentation names every element I made public. Decision surface-members-listed-at-need: 'its checker lists them again to check that the documentation misses none'; artifact-definitions SURFACE-INTENT-DEFINITION: 'its checker, to check the documentation misses no public element and lists no internal one'. Saw: only the planner's listing covers files outside the first checker task's set.

Reviewed /plan-docs source as above. Divergence: only the first checker task of a docspec in round 1 lists the classes (doc-sprint-document.md step 7: 'The first checker task of a docspec in round 1 also lists the classes its `## Lists` names'), and DOC-CHECK-PROMPT makes a listed element the intent keeps internal false only 'Where your brief says to list the docspec's classes'. Every other checker task of the docspec (files seven onward, at 'up to six files each') checks claims against the code alone and reads no surface intent, so an internal or gated entry a writer adds or keeps in those files passes as a held claim (the entry's claims hold against the code). The story promises: reference documentation names no element I kept internal. Artifact-definitions SURFACE-INTENT-DEFINITION: the checker lists the members 'to check the documentation misses no public element and lists no internal one'; decision documentation-claims-checked-until-they-hold has a checker that is not the writer check each claim. Saw: on a reference docspec with more than six files to check, the checker's internal-element check covers only the first task's files; the planner's and the writer's own listing are the only guard on the rest.

body: Reviewed /converge sprint step 3a.2 (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md: 'tests tasks --sprint <path> --stage speed --run <this run's ledger> --round <n> files one speed task for each of the testing.slowest slowest tests of the round that has no speed acceptance at its current test file') and the code it calls in scripts/tests: cmd_tasks passes the --run ledger to stage_speed -> speed_candidates -> speed_rows, where 'items, records = run_items(root, run, "speed"), recorded_tests(root, run)' reads speed verdicts from the certification ledger alone, and speed_settled falls back to state['acceptances'], which only 'tests stamp' writes after the archive. So a test the sprint's build-stage speed task (sprint-document.md step 4, '--stage speed --from state', recorded in the sprint's -run.jsonl) accepted at its current blob, or found product-slow, counts as unsettled in certification and gets a second speed task; a second product-slow verdict also files a second perf: entry for the same site. The verbs also disagree: 'tests slowest --sprint <path> --round <n>' reads run_file(sprint), the sprint's -run.jsonl, so it shows that test settled while '--stage speed --run <ledger>' files it. stamped_acceptances and perf_failures, by contrast, read record_runs (both runs). The story promises: the suite sped up as part of the work already run; decision tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome: 'After a failed whole-suite round ... a speed task reads the testing.slowest slowest tests of the failed round that hold no speed acceptance at their current test file' and 'A speed acceptance ... holds across sprints until the test's own file changes'. Saw (by reading, scripts/tests speed_rows ~line 4399): the build-stage acceptance is ignored inside the same sprint's certification, so readers re-read accepted tests and the batch spends its testing.slowest slots on them instead of on unread slow tests; evidence: speed_rows: 'items, records = run_items(root, run, "speed"), recorded_tests(root, run)'; cmd_slowest: 'speed_candidates(root, sprint, source, run_file(root, sprint))'; record_runs: 'return [run for run in (sibling(sprint, "-run.jsonl"), certification_ledger(root, sprint)) ...]'.

Reviewed the sprint boilerplate's archive step 4 (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md: 'tests stamp ... writes ... the speed ranking') and the next sprint's build-stage speed read (step 4: '--stage speed --from state ... the testing.slowest slowest tests in the ranking the scenario list carries'). In scripts/tests, cmd_stamp calls speed_ranking(..., testing['schedule']['form'], testing['slowest']) and speed_ranking stores 'seconds': values[-keep:], so the carried ranking keeps only the last testing.slowest seconds per test; testing.slowest is declared as 'how many of the slowest tests each run lists, and so the size of each batch a sprint's speed review reads' (ok-setup SKILL.md), not a retention count. Probe in a scratch project (stack run suite-gets-faster-over-time-7c292a1f, true-up'd, one committed test file t/test_a.py), importing .ok-planner/bin/tests and calling speed_ranking on five closed whole-suite rounds of 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 9.0 seconds at the current blob: slowest=1 -> carried 'seconds': [9.0] (median that sprint 1.0); the next sprint's --from state ranking from that carried row -> 'median': 9.0, 'cost': 9.0; slowest=10 -> carried [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 9.0]. The story promises: the suite sped up over the project's life by the work already run; decision tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome: 'The ranking orders the tests by each test's median seconds across the whole-suite rounds that ran it at its current test file's digest', and rejects 'Rank by one round's seconds: machine load in that round reorders the list'. Saw: the carried median spans only the last testing.slowest runs, so with a small batch size the next sprint ranks by one loaded round and points its speed readers at the wrong tests; evidence: 'next sprint --from state: [{... 'seconds': [9.0], 'median': 9.0, 'cost': 9.0}]'.

body: In a scratch project trued up to v30.2.0 with testing on and offers [untested, stale, legacy, runtime]: committed tests/test_z.py (test_z reads tests/data/keep.json) and tests/data/keep.json; `tests offers` printed two groups, legacy:tests and legacy:tests/data. Opened a planning run, took only legacy:tests/data with `tests groups --take legacy:tests/data` (printed "kept: ... tests/test_z.py ... left as they stand"), recorded the sort item the sort prompt asks for (path=tests/data/keep.json sort=support users=["tests/test_z.py::test_z"]), assembled with `tests plan`, then opened the sprint run and ran `tests tasks --stage write`. The story promises: the old tests that guard a promise stay and only the rest are dropped; decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: "A helper, a fixture, or a data file a test that stays uses, adopted or kept, is support, and stays", and the sort prompt: "the assembly keeps a fixture only where a kept test uses it". Saw: the assembly turned the support entry into a deletion though the same plan lists its reader as kept, and the write stage filed a legacy task to delete the file, which leaves the kept test reading a missing file. Evidence: `tests plan --show`: "- `tests/data/keep.json`: delete, orphan; read by tests/test_z.py::test_z. no kept test uses it" and under "## Test files kept as they stand": "- `tests/test_z.py`: no scenario claims it, and its folder was not taken, so a later sprint may take it"; legacy task brief: "legacy file tests/data/keep.json. delete the whole file: orphan." Cause: scripts/tests sorted_support() is fed kept_uses(by_id.values(), ...), which lists only scenarios with a kept action, never the plan's kept test files (groups["kept"]); plan_failures' support-deletion refusal reads the same scenario-only list.

In the same scratch project (testing on; unsorted legacy files other/test_x.py, tests/test_y.py, tests/test_z.py, tests/data/keep.json, none in the scenario list's kept list): planned a sprint that took no offer group and changed no tested story, as an owner who declines the legacy offer for now. `tests groups --sprint <s> --from-run <run>` printed "nothing to plan" and "kept: 4 test files no scenario claims outside the taken folders, left as they stand", and wrote no -plan.json, as plan-sprint SKILL.md section 10 step 1 says ("the sprint plans no tests: write the ## Tests section ... Plan: none: nothing to plan"). Then, following the sprint template step 3/4 (test stages open under testing on "whether or not the sprint plans tests"): `tests tasks --stage write` filed nothing, `tests stray --sprint <s>` listed all four files, and `tests tasks --stage sweep` filed sweep task t1 with brief "stray test files: other/test_x.py, tests/data/keep.json, tests/test_y.py, tests/test_z.py", whose prompt says "Otherwise delete it: git rm <file>". The story promises: keep the old tests that guard a promise and leave no rule they enforced unchecked; decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: "Every sprint's plan, whatever testing.offers lists and under on or frozen, records as kept each test file no scenario claims and no taken folder covers, so review certified never refuses a test file the plan left alone" and "Every test file outside the taken folders stays as it stands". Saw: with no plan file, the kept list `groups` printed is recorded nowhere, so stray (which reads kept only from the plan and test-state.json) lists the untaken legacy suite and the sweep deletes it unsorted, promise-guarding tests and rule-enforcing tests alike; where the sweep is not run (testing frozen, no test stages), `review certified` fails item 3 on the stray files, blocking the sprint. Evidence: `tests stray` output "- other/test_x.py / - tests/data/keep.json / - tests/test_y.py / - tests/test_z.py"; `tests tasks --stage sweep` printed {"role": "sweep", "key": "sweep:1", "task": "t1"}; `python3 -c ...test-state.json kept` printed []. Cause: scripts/tests stray_paths() takes kept from sprint_plan() (the -plan.json, or state kept when none) and ignores the -groups.json kept list the nothing-to-plan path writes.

Same drive and cause as the keep failure on this surface (fingerprint story-retire-a-legacy-suite-.ok-planner/bin/tests-keep): a sprint whose `tests groups` prints "nothing to plan" writes no -plan.json, so `tests stray` lists every untaken legacy test file and the sweep task is told to delete them. tests/test_y.py (test_y asserts "import os" not in app/calc.py, a rule on the code's shape) was among the files the sweep brief named for deletion, with no port. The story promises: the old suite does not leave a rule it enforced unchecked; decision: "A test that enforces a rule on the code's shape ... is ported" and only in folders the owner takes. Saw: the rule-enforcing test goes to the sweep for deletion, so its rule loses its check with no port and no inferred-rule record. Evidence: sweep brief "stray test files: other/test_x.py, tests/data/keep.json, tests/test_y.py, tests/test_z.py".

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/tests-sort.md tells the sort agent: "You do not decide whether the file stays: the assembly keeps a fixture only where a kept test uses it, as that test's support, and deletes it where none does." Decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: "A helper, a fixture, or a data file a test that stays uses, adopted or kept, is support, and stays." In a scratch git project whose .gitignore holds '.claude/' (so the vendored layer is untracked), trued up to v30.2.0 with the working tree's core, I appended a hand-written line to the stamped .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md, then ran 'true-up diagnose' and the bare 'true-up'; the story promises: the owner learns which of their files an upgrade would rewrite and can turn it down, and the decision true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps marks destructive every rewrite of 'a file a person edited, which is every file but a suite-owned file that still carries its stamp ... and holds no uncommitted or staged-only change', since only a rewrite of a file 'whose every change git holds in a commit destroys nothing git cannot restore'; saw: diagnose printed the rewrite as a plain DRIFT step, so the plan held no destructive step, the bare true-up ran with no question and no archive copy, and the hand edit is gone; the same holds in a project with no git repository. evidence: 'DRIFT: stale: .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md differs from the carried v30.2.0 rendering' / 'PLAN: 1 step(s), 0 destructive; plan 1d7ce43f24e6'; bare true-up exit 0 with 'materialized: 1 files under .ok-planner/ and .claude/ (v30.2.0)' and 'Trued up ok-planner at .../p2 (v30.2.0).'; afterwards 'grep -c "My own coding rule" .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md' printed 0 and .ok-planner/history/ held no copy. The tracked-file case works: an uncommitted edit to a tracked stamped file gave 'DESTRUCTIVE: archives a copy of .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md as it stands ...' and the bare true-up refused with 'nothing written'.

Review of /ok (plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md step 4) with the administration document it follows and the true-up core it calls. ADMINISTRATION.md line 47 reads: 'A stale file git does not track, every file in a project with no git repository, and every file under .ok-planner/dashboard/ or .ok-planner/.cache/ stays a DRIFT: step ... True-up writes them all', and the core does the same (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up materialize_steps: only a path in 'uncommitted(...)' gets the archive copy and the destructive mark; any other differing path gets the plain 'stale:' step). SKILL.md step 4.4 then says 'A plan with no destructive step needs no question.' The decision true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps defines destructive as a rewrite of 'every file but a suite-owned file that still carries its stamp or its fixed content and holds no uncommitted or staged-only change' and justifies the exemption only for 'a suite-owned file whose every change git holds in a commit'; the story promises the owner can turn down an upgrade once they know which of their files it would rewrite. A stamped file a person edited where git does not track it (an ignored .claude/, or no repository) is rewritten with no question and no archive copy, so the owner never gets the chance to turn it down. Driven on the core: 'DRIFT: stale: .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md differs from the carried v30.2.0 rendering' / 'PLAN: 1 step(s), 0 destructive', and the bare true-up overwrote the hand edit.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:{{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}. What the code does: for a documentation sprint, once the handoff's commits are made, it writes git rev-parse HEAD into the Window's 'Planned against commit' line unconditionally (shared.md:555-559, 'write the output of git rev-parse HEAD into its Window's Planned against commit line in place of the commit the plan recorded: those commits hold only what the plan already read from the tree'). Trigger: between /plan-docs step 2 (plan-docs/SKILL.md, 'Record the commit: git rev-parse HEAD') and the handoff, the owner commits a change to a file a planned docspec references, or edits such a file after the window ran so the handoff itself commits it. Harm (C1, work item 6 not reached): the rewritten line names a commit that already contains the change the plan never read; docs start (docs:cmd_start) sees planned == HEAD and passes, cmd_stamp's later_commits_bearing measures from the rewritten commit, every planned docspec is stamped at the archive commit, and the next docs window never sees the change, so the docspec can stand current, which work item 6 forbids ('A product commit made between the plan's commit and the run's start stays in the next /plan-docs window for every docspec it bears on'). The rewrite sentence is new in this change. Reports: i21.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp. What the code does: it computes the stale ledger claims from git diff old_stamp..base only ('between = git(root, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "--relative", old_stamp, base, "--")', then stale_claims), keeps every other claim through ledger_after, and stamps a docspec not in later_commits_bearing's set at --commit. later_commits_bearing reads commits up to the parent of --commit, but only through change_reasons (docspec, references, declaring files, Where), never a claim's own 'sources'. Trigger: a documentation sprint stops midway, the owner commits a change to a file a kept ledger claim lists in its sources and the docspec's References do not cover, then a new /goal resumes with the base kept (work item 7, B27). Harm (A8, decision documentation-claim-ledger: 'the ledger never holds a claim no checker confirmed at its stamp'): the ledger keeps the claim as held at the new stamp after its source changed, and the next docs window diffs from that stamp and never marks it stale. The stale diff stood at the base, but the resume that keeps the base and puts owner commits between base and the archive commit is new in this change, so the change newly exposes it. Reports: i22.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:current_section. What the code does: for each non-equal diff hunk between a live sprint's section and the carried template, it keeps the old lines unchanged where they hold no retired line ('held = sum(1 for line in old if line in retired)'; 'if equal or not held: out.extend(old); continue'). A hunk that is a pure insertion in the carried template has old == [], holds no retired line, and its carried lines are never written. Trigger: an owner trues up a project holding a live sprint laid out by v30.2.0 that stopped mid-run, then starts /goal. Evidence: running the copied current_section over the v30.2.0 template's How to execute section against the current template and retired-boilerplate.json leaves the result unequal to the carried text; missing are step 4's 'On a resumed run, file no stage twice. File no build task for a work item ...', step 6's 'On a resumed run, build the checklist from the run ...', and the test-stage paragraphs (step 3's 'Where step 2 found that the run opens its test stages, open them: ...', step 4's --stage write/verify/sweep/speed paragraph, step 7's and step 10's additions). The Completion contract comes out current. Harm (R2, B24/B26 ruling 'migrate: true-up rewrites the boilerplate from retired-boilerplate.json ... with no code change'): the migrated sprint's step 3 now runs tasks use and tasks retry --all, then step 4, lacking the resume rule, files one build task per stage again, so two build tasks write the same files; step 2 names test stages that step 3 no longer opens. Scope: the migration this sprint rules relies on current_section, and its new step 4 and step 6 lines are pure insertions. Reports: i23.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:planned_commit. What the code does: it matches the Window line with PLANNED_COMMIT = re.compile(r"^Planned against commit `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`\.$") (docs:100), which takes no 64-hex name. Trigger: a project whose git repository uses SHA-256 object names (git init --object-format=sha256; review:default_base, new in this sprint, names such repositories as supported). /plan-docs records git rev-parse HEAD (plan-docs/SKILL.md step 2) and the handoff rewrites the line to HEAD, both 64 hex. Path: documentation sprint step 3 -> docs:cmd_start -> held_planned_commit -> planned_commit returns None -> InputError '<sprint> holds no "Planned against commit `<sha>`." line under ## Window; plan the documentation sprint again with /plan-docs', exit 1, and the run stops. Harm (A3): no documentation sprint can start in such a repository, and the message is false, since the plan holds the line and planning again writes the same line. At the base the documentation sprint had no start check. Same class in the same file: SHA = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$") (docs:104), which cmd_stamp uses on --commit; siblings that stood at the base and the change does not reach: review:CLOSED_STAMP (review:75), tests:SHA (tests:563), discover:823. Reports: i24.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/tests.md:{{TEST-PLANNER-REVIEW-PROMPT}} and {{TEST-PLAN-WIDE-REVIEW-PROMPT}}. What the code does: each prompt pastes {{TEST-WASTE-RULE}} (tests.md:53, tests.md:162), which after B4 names seed data as a waste only 'where the project has a seed `testing.setup` builds' (shared.md:777-779), but neither prompt's Read list (tests.md:60-84, 170-190) reads testing.setup or .ok-planner/config.json. The sibling users B4 names were updated: tests-story.md:83 and tests-runtime.md:52 read testing.setup, and test-speed.md gained Read step 5 for it. Trigger: /plan-sprint plans tests in a project with no seed (testing.setup null). Harm (R3, B4 'rewrite' left a user behind): a planner reviewer or the plan-wide reviewer has no input to evaluate the condition and can send a scenario back for 'data the test only reads that the seed could hold', naming a seed the project lacks, which decision:seed-recommended-never-required and work item 1 ('no test-stage prompt or rule names a seed') rule out. Reports: i25.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:main. What the code does: main runs project_root(), load_config(root), and run_under_project_python before args.run (review:2333-2339), and load_config raises ReviewError on a missing or unreadable .ok-planner/review/config.json or one that declares no block_sources/standards/python/prompts_dir (review:152-163), so cmd_certified never reaches its stop check (review:2118-2120); the module also loads issues at import (review:28 'issues = load_sibling("issues")', which loads tasks), so with .ok-planner/bin/tasks missing the tool dies at import. Trigger: the sprint template's step 2 (sprint-document.md:124-129) names pre-run stops for 'the review estate lacks the .ok-planner/review/config.json the command reads' and for a missing task tracker, and stops each 'as step 11 says': write -stopped.txt, then run review certified. Harm (C4, decision every-stop-ends-the-goal, 'Every stop the executor makes before a sprint's contract holds ends the goal: a stop before the run files its first task ... At each, the session writes a stop record ... then runs review certified, which, while the record stands, prints SPRINT STOPPED'): review certified prints 'review: cannot read ...' or a traceback and exits 1, never SPRINT STOPPED, so a /goal checker keeps pushing a stopped run. Work item 7 asked for these stops and for the stop check after the config load. Reports: i26.

Work item 6 (a product commit made between the plan's commit and the run's start stays in the next window; docs window never reports such a docspec current) is reached only in part. Entry point: /plan-docs step 2 (SKILL.md:26) records git rev-parse HEAD as the Window's 'Planned against commit' and computes the window then; the planners read the tree after it. The handoff (shared.md, PLANNING-HANDOFF, the paragraph after the commits) then overwrites that line with git rev-parse HEAD after its commits, on the claim that 'those commits hold only what the plan already read from the tree'. That claim does not hold: (a) any commit the owner made out of band between step 2 and the handoff is now an ancestor of the rewritten line, and (b) the handoff commits every path git status lists outside .ok-planner/ at handoff time, including an edit made after step 2's window. Trigger: the owner commits a change to a file a planned docspec references (or edits it uncommitted, which the handoff then commits) while the /plan-docs session runs past step 2, and the handoff makes a commit. Path: handoff rewrites Window to HEAD -> doc-sprint step 3 docs:cmd_start sees planned == HEAD and prints 'start: ... no commit follows the plan', exit 0 -> base = HEAD -> docs:cmd_stamp later_commits_bearing finds planned == parent of the archive commit, returns no bearing -> every planned docspec stamped at the archive commit -> the next docs window diffs from that stamp and never sees the change, so the docspec can stand current. Outcome: the commit the work item names is stamped over. Scope: caused by the change (the rewrite is new in this sprint, from the notes review of work item 6).

Rule: decision documentation-claim-ledger, 'the ledger never holds a claim no checker confirmed at its stamp' (and the USAGE text 'Every claim in the ledger held at the stamp'). cmd_stamp computes the stale set of kept ledger claims from git diff old_stamp..base (docs:cmd_stamp, 'between = git(root, "diff", ..., old_stamp, base, "--")'), then, for a docspec not in later['bearing'], stamps it at args.commit. A commit landing between the base and the parent of --commit is never counted against kept claims. later_commits_bearing only moves the stamp back for a docspec the window reasons (change_reasons: docspec, corpus/code references, declaring files, documentation paths) bear on; a claim's own 'sources' can name a file outside those, which stale_claims checks but change_reasons does not. Trigger: a documentation sprint stops midway (step 8 / CEREMONY-RUN-RULES), the owner commits a change to a file a kept ledger claim lists in its sources but that the docspec's References do not cover, and a new /goal resumes; docs start passes (no window reason fires), the base is kept (B27 resume), and the claim's file is not rewritten. Path: doc-sprint step 3 keeps base -> run completes -> archive commit X -> docs:cmd_stamp: stale over old_stamp..base misses the commit -> ledger_after keeps the claim -> state['stamp'] = X. Harm: the ledger holds, stamped at X, a claim no checker confirmed after its source changed, and the next docs window diffs from X and never marks it stale. Scope: the code stood at the base, and the change reaches it: resume keeping the base (B27, work item 7) is new in this sprint and is the step that puts owner commits between the base and the archive commit, and work item 6 changed cmd_stamp to read commits up to the parent of --commit for the stamp alone, not for the ledger.

B26 (and B24's test-tools half) ruling: 'migrate: true-up rewrites the boilerplate from retired-boilerplate.json ... with no code change'. What an old user gets: current_section (true-up:2147) replaces a non-equal hunk only where the live sprint's old lines hold a retired line ('if equal or not held: out.extend(old); continue'). A hunk that is a pure insertion in the carried template (old = []) holds no retired line, so its carried lines are never written. File no build task for a work item some build task's --cites already names ...'; step 6 loses 'On a resumed run, build the checklist from the run ...'; and the test-stage text a124cfa added (step 3 'Where step 2 found that the run opens its test stages, open them: ...' with its prompt registrations and pool config, step 4's whole '--stage write/verify/sweep/speed' paragraph, step 7's test-stage refile and refusal paragraph, step 10's calls-pool sentence) never lands. Trigger: an owner trues up a project holding a sprint an earlier release planned that stopped mid-run, then starts /goal. Old outcome (base): no resume at all. New outcome: step 3 now runs 'tasks use' and 'tasks retry --all', then step 4, lacking the resume rule, files one build task per stage again, so two build tasks of one stage write the same files; and step 2 now says the run 'opens its test stages (step 3)' while step 3 carries no test-stage opening. The doc-sprint kind simulates clean (v30.2.0, v29.0.0). Scope: current_section stood at base; the change reaches it, because the sprint's B24/B26 migration relies on it and its new step 4 and step 6 lines are pure insertions; the a124cfa half stood at base, unreleased, and ships in the same release.

A3. Trigger: a project whose git repository uses SHA-256 object names (git init --object-format=sha256; the sprint's own review::default_base call names such repositories as supported). Path: /plan-docs records 'git rev-parse HEAD' (plan-docs/SKILL.md:26) into the Window's 'Planned against commit `<sha>`.' line, and {{PLANNING-HANDOFF}} (skills/_sprint/shared.md, new text) rewrites that line to 'git rev-parse HEAD' after its commits; both write a 64-hex name. Documentation sprint step 3 then runs docs::cmd_start -> held_planned_commit -> planned_commit, whose pattern is PLANNED_COMMIT = re.compile(r"^Planned against commit `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`\.$") (scripts/docs:100). It matches no 64-hex line, so cmd_start raises '<sprint> holds no "Planned against commit `<sha>`." line under ## Window; plan the documentation sprint again with /plan-docs', exit 1, and step 3 stops the run with 'docs start: the plan must be made again'. Harm: the plan does hold the line, so the message is false. Planning again writes the same 64-hex line, so no documentation sprint can start in such a repository. Base: docs had no start check and read no planned commit, so a doc sprint ran. Scope: caused by the change (work item 6).

B4 (rewrite): {{TEST-WASTE-RULE}} now names seed data as a waste only 'where the project has a seed `testing.setup` builds'. Users: the B4 notes name tests.md among the planning prompts. tests.md carries the rule in {{TEST-PLANNER-REVIEW-PROMPT}} (tests.md:53) and {{TEST-PLAN-WIDE-REVIEW-PROMPT}} (tests.md:162). Neither prompt's Read list (tests.md:60-84 and 170-190) reads `testing.setup` or .ok-planner/config.json. The sprint did update the other users: tests-story.md:83 and tests-runtime.md:52 read testing.setup, and test-speed.md got a new Read step 5 for it. Goal and source: decision:seed-recommended-never-required and work item 1 say that, where the project has no seed, no reader names a seed and no test-stage prompt or rule names one. What the reviewers get now is a condition they have no input to evaluate. In a seedless project, a planner reviewer or the plan-wide reviewer can still send a scenario back with 'data the test only reads that the seed could hold', which reopens the seed suggestion the owner ruled out. For a reopened, unissued test task tX it adds the holders of its own files to its waits, tests:4133 'waits |= {holders[path] for path in task.get("files") or [] if path in holders}', and discards only tX itself. holders_of maps each path to the latest open holder, so where a later open test task tY (filed after [tX] on the same test file F) or a legacy task holds F, holders[F] = tY and planned_after(tX, {..., tY}) asks tasks task set to make tX wait on tY, which waits on tX: tasks:check_dependencies fails 'task tX would wait on itself through ...' (tasks:724-726). Trigger: two scenarios in one test file, both test tasks closed blocked with support items (or tY running/partial), the run stops, and the resume runs tasks retry --all then tests tasks --stage write. Harm (A3): --stage write raises after it already filed the support tasks earlier in the filings list, and every later --stage write computes the same waits and fails the same way, so the resumed run can never pass the write stage. At base the branch ran only for closed-blocked tasks, which holders_of skips. Report: i9.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write (blocked_on_support loop) with stage_support. Rule: decision:test-support-written-before-tests ('a support task makes the change before the test task runs again'), which the notes' resume call applies to a reopened test task. stage_support briefs an open support item only where 'path not in held' (tests:4005-4006) and its path is non-empty; the loop's skip for an unbriefed item applies only to a closed-blocked task (tests:4128 'if closed_blocked(task) and any(... not in briefed ...)'). For a reopened, unissued task T whose open item I is at a path P held by an open support task S1 that does not cite I, waits = {latest_support[P]} = {S1} and planned_after(T, {S1}); for an item with no path, waits is empty and 'elif waits:' adds nothing. Trigger: resume (tasks retry --all reopens T and S1) then tests tasks --stage write. Harm: when S1 closes (or at once, for a pathless item), close's step issues T, which runs again before any support task has made I, the reverse of the order the decision commits to; the next --stage write no longer sees T (reopened_on_support needs 'not task.get("issued")'). At base a closed-blocked task in this case waited until I was briefed. Report: i10.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write with stage_support. WI 7 ('The session files no stage twice'; notes: 'file no task whose role and key the run already holds') not reached on a resumed documentation sprint. Step 5 says: 'On a resumed run, here and in steps 6 and 7, file no task whose role and key the run already holds, as tasks status lists them.' tasks status (scripts/tasks cmd_status) prints only open tasks ('for t in open_tasks: print("open ...")', open_tasks = state != closed) plus the ids of closed retryable tasks; a task that closed done is never listed, in text or --json. Path: step 4 on resume -> tasks use -> tasks retry --all reopens every task that did not close done -> step 5 reads tasks status, which lists those reopened tasks and none of the done ones -> every write item whose writer task already closed done is absent from the listing, so the session files a second writer task with the same role and key (tasks file refuses no duplicate key); steps 6 and 7 likewise refile done style and checker tasks. The writer reruns on a document already written and checked, and its claims are recorded again. Step 7's 'the loop goes on from the highest round the run records' has the same gap: the round lives in closed checker task keys (<slug>:<round>:<n>), which tasks status does not show (its 'round:' line is the tracker's own round, which this run never sets). Scope: caused (the resume rule is new).

WI 7 ('every stop must end the goal') not reached on one pre-run stop step 3 names. Step 3: 'First check .ok-planner/bin/tasks, .ok-planner/bin/docs, and the profile ok-opus ...: a missing one is the front door's administration (/ok) to materialize, so stop and say so', and every stop goes 'as {{CEREMONY-RUN-RULES}} says': write the stop record, then 'run .ok-planner/bin/docs complete --sprint <path>, show its output whole, and stop'. Where the missing tool is .ok-planner/bin/docs itself, that command cannot run, so no DOCS STOPPED line ever appears in the session. Step 1's stop condition, stated to /goal's checker, which reads only the session, ends the goal only on DOCS COMPLETE or DOCS STOPPED printed by that command; the goal rule says the same. So on this stop the checker sees neither line and the goal keeps looping, the exact harm WI 7 names ('runs have stopped while the goal kept looping and spending tokens'). The builder recorded this as divergence call i24 and left it. The sprint template has the same gap for a missing .ok-planner/bin/review (outside this pass's area; noted for the merge agent). Scope: caused (the stop-record mechanism and its goal line are new).

Entry A1. cmd_refile promises (USAGE) that 'every open task that waited on the task waits on the refile too', but it only appends the refile's id to each open waiter's after (tasks:1049-1050) and leaves its issued=1 as it stands. A waiter's issued was set when the source closed (cmd_close -> step -> ready() counts any close, tasks:786-791), and cmd_claim checks issued alone (tasks:1106), so the waiter stays claimable before the refile runs. Trigger on WI 3's own path: sprint step 7 refiles a build B1 that closed partial ('tasks refile <task> --files <its files and that path>'); B2, chained after B1 because their files overlap, was issued when B1 closed and is claimed beside the refile: two writers on one file. Also: the refile copies the source's after as it stands (tasks:1035), not each dependency's latest refile, so refiling a blocked B2 whose after names a refiled B1 waits on the closed B1, not its open refile. I1 fixed the issued-waiter half of this class in cmd_retry only (retry_records un-issues waiters). Scope: stood at base; reached by the change (WI 3 changed cmd_refile and step 7 now routes through it).

Evidence: cmd_refile appends the refile's id to each open waiter's after (tasks:1049-1050) and leaves its issued=1, which cmd_close's step set when the source closed (ready counts any close, tasks:786-791), and cmd_claim checks issued alone, so a waiter whose files overlap is claimed beside the refile. body: Reviewed /plan-docs and drove its documentation sprint's steps against a scratch project (true-up of the working tree, one docspec 'usage' whose Where is docs/usage.md, a plan with one 'check' item). Followed steps 4-8 of the template exactly: checker t1 recorded one held and one false claim in docs/usage.md; per step 7 a fix writer t2 edited docs/usage.md and set the claim open; checker t3 held the rewrite and set the old claim replaced; step 8 wrote the report and ran docs complete. The story promises: a way to bring every document up to date whenever the owner chooses, so a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands, with the run going unattended to completion (decision documentation-sprints-write-the-documentation: 'the plan runs unattended to completion'). Saw: the template's own steps end in a state its own contract refuses. - i42: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:{{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}. What the code does: for a documentation sprint, once the handoff's commits are made, it writes git rev-parse HEAD into the Window's 'Planned against commit' line unconditionally (shared.md:555-559, 'write the output of git rev-parse HEAD into its Window's Planned against commit line in place of the commit the plan recorded: those commits hold only what the plan already read from the tree'). Trigger: between /plan-docs step 2 (plan-docs/SKILL.md, 'Record the commit: git rev-parse HEAD') and the handoff, the owner commits a change to a file a planned docspec references, or edits such a file after the window ran so the handoff itself commits it. Harm (C1, work item 6 not reached): the rewritten line names a commit that already contains the change the plan never read; docs start (docs:cmd_start) sees planned == HEAD and passes, cmd_stamp's later_commits_bearing measures from the rewritten commit, every planned docspec is stamped at the archive commit, and the next docs window never sees the change, so the docspec can stand current, which work item 6 forbids ('A product commit made between the plan's commit and the run's start stays in the next /plan-docs window for every docspec it bears on'). The rewrite sentence is new in this change. Reports: i21.

What the code does: it computes the stale ledger claims from git diff old_stamp..base only ('between = git(root, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "--relative", old_stamp, base, "--")', then stale_claims), keeps every other claim through ledger_after, and stamps a docspec not in later_commits_bearing's set at --commit. later_commits_bearing reads commits up to the parent of --commit, but only through change_reasons (docspec, references, declaring files, Where), never a claim's own 'sources'. brief:

- i60: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:{{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}. Work item 6: 'A product commit made between the plan's commit and the run's start stays in the next /plan-docs window for every docspec it bears on'. The handoff says 'For a documentation sprint, once the commits are made, write the output of git rev-parse HEAD into its Window's Planned against commit line in place of the commit the plan recorded: those commits hold only what the plan already read from the tree' (shared.md:555-559). The claim does not hold: a commit the owner makes out of band after /plan-docs step 2 recorded HEAD (plan-docs SKILL.md:26), or an edit made after step 2's window that the handoff then commits, becomes an ancestor of the rewritten line. Trigger: the owner commits, or edits and the handoff commits, a file a planned docspec references during the session after step 2. Path: the rewrite moves the line to HEAD -> docs:cmd_start sees planned == HEAD and exits 0 -> cmd_stamp's later_commits_bearing measures from the rewritten commit and stamps every planned docspec at the archive commit. Harm: the next docs window starts after a commit the plan never read and can report the docspec it bears on current. Caused (the rewrite is new). Report: i17. Related: i18 (the no branch).
- i61: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_start, reached from the {{PLANNING-HANDOFF}} no branch. On the owner's no (or paths still standing after the commits, 'go on as on a no'), the handoff names the paths and says 'execution's base step refuses to start while any such path stands uncommitted', hands over no goal line, and leaves the Window line as recorded (the rewrite runs only 'once the commits are made', shared.md:555). The owner commits those paths by hand, as directed, and runs /goal. Doc-sprint step 3 runs docs start; the owner's commits change the files the window reached the docspec on, so cmd_start prints 'The plan does not cover these commits, so the plan must be made again with /plan-docs before the run files a task.' and exits 2, and step 3 writes the stop record 'docs start: the plan must be made again'. Harm (A9): the message is false: docs window read the working tree (changed_since diffs the stamp against the tree plus untracked files, docs:169-172), so the plan read exactly those changes; the owner acts on it by discarding a valid, approved plan. Before the change the same sequence recorded the base and ran. Caused (docs start and the step 3 stop are new). Report: i18.
- i62: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/doc-sprint-document.md:How to execute, step 5 (and steps 6 and 7). Work item 7 ('The session files no stage twice'; notes: 'file no task whose role and key the run already holds'). Step 5 says 'On a resumed run, here and in steps 6 and 7, file no task whose role and key the run already holds, as tasks status lists them' (doc-sprint-document.md:119). tasks:cmd_status prints only open tasks ('open_tasks = [t for t in tasks if t["state"] != CLOSED]', tasks:1517, text and --json) plus retryable ids; a task that closed done is never listed. Step 7's 'the loop goes on from the highest round the run records' has the same gap: the round lives in closed checker task keys, and status's 'round:' line is the tracker's own round. Trigger: a resumed documentation sprint after retry --all. Harm: the session files a second writer, style, or checker task for each work item whose task closed done, so a writer reruns on a document already written and checked. Caused (the resume rule is new). Report: i19.
- i63: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/doc-sprint-document.md:How to execute, steps 1 and 3. Work item 7 ('every stop must end the goal'). Step 3: 'First check .ok-planner/bin/tasks, .ok-planner/bin/docs, and the profile ok-opus ...: a missing one is the front door's administration (/ok) to materialize, so stop and say so', and every stop goes through {{CEREMONY-RUN-RULES}}: write the stop record, then run .ok-planner/bin/docs complete --sprint <path> (shared.md:452). Where the missing tool is .ok-planner/bin/docs itself, that command cannot run (and docs loads review at import, docs:125, which loads issues and tasks, so a missing tracker or review crashes it too). Step 1's stop condition ends the goal only on DOCS COMPLETE or DOCS STOPPED printed by that command. Trigger: /goal on a documentation sprint in a project missing bin/docs (or bin/review or bin/tasks). Harm: no DOCS STOPPED line appears, so the checker keeps the goal looping, the harm work item 7 names; the outcome is reached only in part. Builder call i24 recorded the gap. Sibling in sprint-4: the sprint template's pre-run stops (i52). Report: i20.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i44
- i44: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:current_section. What the code does: for each non-equal diff hunk between a live sprint's section and the carried template, it keeps the old lines unchanged where they hold no retired line ('held = sum(1 for line in old if line in retired)'; 'if equal or not held: out.extend(old); continue'). A hunk that is a pure insertion in the carried template has old == [], holds no retired line, and its carried lines are never written. Trigger: an owner trues up a project holding a live sprint laid out by v30.2.0 that stopped mid-run, then starts /goal. Evidence: running the copied current_section over the v30.2.0 template's How to execute section against the current template and retired-boilerplate.json leaves the result unequal to the carried text; missing are step 4's 'On a resumed run, file no stage twice. File no build task for a work item ...', step 6's 'On a resumed run, build the checklist from the run ...', and the test-stage paragraphs (step 3's 'Where step 2 found that the run opens its test stages, open them: ...', step 4's --stage write/verify/sweep/speed paragraph, step 7's and step 10's additions). The Completion contract comes out current. Harm (R2, B24/B26 ruling 'migrate: true-up rewrites the boilerplate from retired-boilerplate.json ... with no code change'): the migrated sprint's step 3 now runs tasks use and tasks retry --all, then step 4, lacking the resume rule, files one build task per stage again, so two build tasks write the same files; step 2 names test stages that step 3 no longer opens. Scope: the migration this sprint rules relies on current_section, and its new step 4 and step 6 lines are pure insertions. Reports: i23.
