- i47: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:main. What the code does: main runs project_root(), load_config(root), and run_under_project_python before args.run (review:2333-2339), and load_config raises ReviewError on a missing or unreadable .ok-planner/review/config.json or one that declares no block_sources/standards/python/prompts_dir (review:152-163), so cmd_certified never reaches its stop check (review:2118-2120); the module also loads issues at import (review:28 'issues = load_sibling("issues")', which loads tasks), so with .ok-planner/bin/tasks missing the tool dies at import. Trigger: the sprint template's step 2 (sprint-document.md:124-129) names pre-run stops for 'the review estate lacks the .ok-planner/review/config.json the command reads' and for a missing task tracker, and stops each 'as step 11 says': write -stopped.txt, then run review certified. Harm (C4, decision every-stop-ends-the-goal, 'Every stop the executor makes before a sprint's contract holds ends the goal: a stop before the run files its first task ... At each, the session writes a stop record ... then runs review certified, which, while the record stands, prints SPRINT STOPPED'): review certified prints 'review: cannot read ...' or a traceback and exits 1, never SPRINT STOPPED, so a /goal checker keeps pushing a stopped run. Work item 7 asked for these stops and for the stop check after the config load. Reports: i26.
- i51: Site: .ok-planner/review/project.md:Scripts (tests entry). The facts say 'Where testing.enabled is off, groups, plan, reached, slowest, reports, settled, tasks --stage speed, and run --sprint refuse'. Since this sprint, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write calls testing_config(root, sprint) (tests:4085, 'testing = testing_config(root, sprint)', added for work item 1's seed rule, notes item 1 'stage_write ... reads testing'), and testing_config raises under off with a sprint (tests:753-756), so tasks --stage write refuses too; at base stage_write read no testing. Trigger: a driver or reviewer reading the facts to judge tests tasks --stage write under testing.enabled off. Harm (A9): the facts the review loop pastes into every prompt state a verb list that is not so, and readers judge refusals against it. Report: i1.
- i52: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:main (with the sprint template's step 2, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md). Work item 7 and decision:every-stop-ends-the-goal ('a stop before the run files its first task' ends the goal through review certified printing SPRINT STOPPED). Step 2 names pre-run stops that route through step 11's 'write the stop record, then run review certified', where review certified cannot reach its stop check: (1) 'review approved refuses ... the review estate lacks the .ok-planner/review/config.json the command reads': review:main runs load_config(root) and run_under_project_python before args.run (review:2336-2339), and load_config raises 'cannot read .ok-planner/review/config.json' or 'declares no <key>' (review:152-163), so certified exits 1 before cmd_certified reaches stop_reason; (2) the tracker check 'a missing one is ... (/ok) to materialize, so stop': review loads issues at import (review:28 'issues = load_sibling("issues")') and issues loads tasks at import, so with .ok-planner/bin/tasks missing review dies with an uncaught FileNotFoundError traceback. brief:
fix round 1; defects i54 i55 i56
- i54: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write (the reopened-task branch of the blocked_on_support loop). For a reopened, unissued test task tX it adds the holders of its own files to its waits, tests:4133 'waits |= {holders[path] for path in task.get("files") or [] if path in holders}', and discards only tX itself. holders_of maps each path to the latest open holder, so where a later open test task tY (filed after [tX] on the same test file F) or a legacy task holds F, holders[F] = tY and planned_after(tX, {..., tY}) asks tasks task set to make tX wait on tY, which waits on tX: tasks:check_dependencies fails 'task tX would wait on itself through ...' (tasks:724-726). Trigger: two scenarios in one test file, both test tasks closed blocked with support items (or tY running/partial), the run stops, and the resume runs tasks retry --all then tests tasks --stage write. Harm (A3): --stage write raises after it already filed the support tasks earlier in the filings list, and every later --stage write computes the same waits and fails the same way, so the resumed run can never pass the write stage. At base the branch ran only for closed-blocked tasks, which holders_of skips. Report: i9.
- i55: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write (blocked_on_support loop) with stage_support. Rule: decision:test-support-written-before-tests ('a support task makes the change before the test task runs again'), which the notes' resume call applies to a reopened test task. stage_support briefs an open support item only where 'path not in held' (tests:4005-4006) and its path is non-empty; the loop's skip for an unbriefed item applies only to a closed-blocked task (tests:4128 'if closed_blocked(task) and any(... not in briefed ...)'). For a reopened, unissued task T whose open item I is at a path P held by an open support task S1 that does not cite I, waits = {latest_support[P]} = {S1} and planned_after(T, {S1}); for an item with no path, waits is empty and 'elif waits:' adds nothing. Trigger: resume (tasks retry --all reopens T and S1) then tests tasks --stage write. Harm: when S1 closes (or at once, for a pathless item), close's step issues T, which runs again before any support task has made I, the reverse of the order the decision commits to; the next --stage write no longer sees T (reopened_on_support needs 'not task.get("issued")'). At base a closed-blocked task in this case waited until I was briefed. Report: i10.
- i56: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write with stage_support. Work item 7's resume and the notes call 'On resume, --stage write treats a reopened, unissued test task that has an open support item as blocked on support, and adds the support task it files to that test task's after'. stage_support files no support task for an open item whose path another open support task S0 holds (tests:4005 'path not in held'), or whose path is empty; the loop skips an unbriefed item only for a closed-blocked task (tests:4128), so for the reopened task planned_after adds only latest_support[path] = S0 (tests:4132-4138), or nothing for a pathless item. Trigger: resume, retry --all, then --stage write. Harm: the reopened test task is issued when S0 closes, or at the first next, before the support it recorded exists; the outcome the notes call promises is reached only in part. Same flaw as i55 (sprint-8). Report: i12.

fix round 1; defects i57 i58
- i57: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:retry_records (with ready). retry --all reopens a closed-blocked task B2 keeping its after ['B1'] (reset_task), where B1 closed partial and was refiled as R1, which is open. ready() counts any closed dependency (tasks:786-791), and retry_records un-issues only waiters whose after names a task the set reopens (tasks:1263 'named = sorted(reopened & set(t.get("after") or []))'); it never follows a reopened task's own after to the latest refile. Trigger: B2 chained after B1 for overlapping files; B1 closes partial, step issues B2, B2 closes blocked; the session refiles B1 as R1 (B2 closed, so cmd_refile does not append R1 to B2's after); the run stops; resume runs tasks retry --all. Harm (A1): the drain's next issues B2 beside R1, so two agents write the overlapping files at once and B2 builds before B1's remainder lands. The same root shows where a refile copies a source's after naming a refiled-away dependency (tasks:1035, the second half of i14). Caused: retry --all (work item 7) reopens such a task on every resume. Report: i13.
- i58: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:cmd_retry (single form). I2's refusal fires for every task retry_kind rejects that a refile replaced: 'if kind is None and t["id"] in refiled: fail("task %s was refiled as %s; retry %s" ...)', and refiles_of maps a task only to its immediate refile (tasks:1234-1235). brief:
fix round 1; defects i42 i43 i45 i59
- i42: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:{{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}. What the code does: for a documentation sprint, once the handoff's commits are made, it writes git rev-parse HEAD into the Window's 'Planned against commit' line unconditionally (shared.md:555-559, 'write the output of git rev-parse HEAD into its Window's Planned against commit line in place of the commit the plan recorded: those commits hold only what the plan already read from the tree'). Trigger: between /plan-docs step 2 (plan-docs/SKILL.md, 'Record the commit: git rev-parse HEAD') and the handoff, the owner commits a change to a file a planned docspec references, or edits such a file after the window ran so the handoff itself commits it. Harm (C1, work item 6 not reached): the rewritten line names a commit that already contains the change the plan never read; docs start (docs:cmd_start) sees planned == HEAD and passes, cmd_stamp's later_commits_bearing measures from the rewritten commit, every planned docspec is stamped at the archive commit, and the next docs window never sees the change, so the docspec can stand current, which work item 6 forbids ('A product commit made between the plan's commit and the run's start stays in the next /plan-docs window for every docspec it bears on'). The rewrite sentence is new in this change. Reports: i21.
- i43: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp. What the code does: it computes the stale ledger claims from git diff old_stamp..base only ('between = git(root, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "--relative", old_stamp, base, "--")', then stale_claims), keeps every other claim through ledger_after, and stamps a docspec not in later_commits_bearing's set at --commit. later_commits_bearing reads commits up to the parent of --commit, but only through change_reasons (docspec, references, declaring files, Where), never a claim's own 'sources'. Trigger: a documentation sprint stops midway, the owner commits a change to a file a kept ledger claim lists in its sources and the docspec's References do not cover, then a new /goal resumes with the base kept (work item 7, B27). Harm (A8, decision documentation-claim-ledger: 'the ledger never holds a claim no checker confirmed at its stamp'): the ledger keeps the claim as held at the new stamp after its source changed, and the next docs window diffs from that stamp and never marks it stale. The stale diff stood at the base, but the resume that keeps the base and puts owner commits between base and the archive commit is new in this change, so the change newly exposes it. Reports: i22.
- i45: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:planned_commit. What the code does: it matches the Window line with PLANNED_COMMIT = re.compile(r"^Planned against commit `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`\.$") (docs:100), which takes no 64-hex name. Trigger: a project whose git repository uses SHA-256 object names (git init --object-format=sha256; review:default_base, new in this sprint, names such repositories as supported). /plan-docs records git rev-parse HEAD (plan-docs/SKILL.md step 2) and the handoff rewrites the line to HEAD, both 64 hex. Path: documentation sprint step 3 -> docs:cmd_start -> held_planned_commit -> planned_commit returns None -> InputError '<sprint> holds no "Planned against commit `<sha>`." line under ## Window; plan the documentation sprint again with /plan-docs', exit 1, and the run stops. Harm (A3): no documentation sprint can start in such a repository, and the message is false, since the plan holds the line and planning again writes the same line. At the base the documentation sprint had no start check. Same class in the same file: SHA = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$") (docs:104), which cmd_stamp uses on --commit; siblings that stood at the base and the change does not reach: review:CLOSED_STAMP (review:75), tests:SHA (tests:563), discover:823. Reports: i24.
- i59: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:bearing_docspecs (used by cmd_start and cmd_stamp through later_commits_bearing). Work item 6: 'docs window never reports such a docspec current'. bearing_docspecs unions change_reasons alone (docs:560-570: docspec file, corpus and code references, declaring files, Where paths), while window_entry also reaches a docspec on its stale claims ('entry["status"] = "reached" if reasons or stale else "current"', stale_claims checks each claim's sources, docs:311-314). Trigger: after the plan's commit, the owner commits a change to a file a planned docspec's ledger claim names in its sources and that no reference, Where, or declaring entry matches. docs start finds no bearing and exits 0; cmd_stamp drops the claim from the ledger as stale (old_stamp..base) while its text stays unchecked, and stamps at --commit since the slug is not in later['bearing']; on a resumed run an owner commit after the base is outside old_stamp..base, so the claim is kept as held. Harm: the next docs window diffs from the archive commit and reports the docspec current over a commit that made a documented claim stale. Caused (bearing_docspecs, cmd_start, later_commits_bearing are new). Report: i16.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i44
- i44: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:current_section. What the code does: for each non-equal diff hunk between a live sprint's section and the carried template, it keeps the old lines unchanged where they hold no retired line ('held = sum(1 for line in old if line in retired)'; 'if equal or not held: out.extend(old); continue'). A hunk that is a pure insertion in the carried template has old == [], holds no retired line, and its carried lines are never written. Trigger: an owner trues up a project holding a live sprint laid out by v30.2.0 that stopped mid-run, then starts /goal. Evidence: running the copied current_section over the v30.2.0 template's How to execute section against the current template and retired-boilerplate.json leaves the result unequal to the carried text; missing are step 4's 'On a resumed run, file no stage twice. File no build task for a work item ...', step 6's 'On a resumed run, build the checklist from the run ...', and the test-stage paragraphs (step 3's 'Where step 2 found that the run opens its test stages, open them: ...', step 4's --stage write/verify/sweep/speed paragraph, step 7's and step 10's additions). The Completion contract comes out current. Harm (R2, B24/B26 ruling 'migrate: true-up rewrites the boilerplate from retired-boilerplate.json ... with no code change'): the migrated sprint's step 3 now runs tasks use and tasks retry --all, then step 4, lacking the resume rule, files one build task per stage again, so two build tasks write the same files; step 2 names test stages that step 3 no longer opens. Scope: the migration this sprint rules relies on current_section, and its new step 4 and step 6 lines are pure insertions. Reports: i23.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:retry_records (with ready). retry --all reopens a closed-blocked task B2 keeping its after ['B1'] (reset_task), where B1 closed partial and was refiled as R1, which is open. ready() counts any closed dependency (tasks:786-791), and retry_records un-issues only waiters whose after names a task the set reopens (tasks:1263 'named = sorted(reopened & set(t.get("after") or []))'); it never follows a reopened task's own after to the latest refile. Trigger: B2 chained after B1 for overlapping files; B1 closes partial, step issues B2, B2 closes blocked; the session refiles B1 as R1 (B2 closed, so cmd_refile does not append R1 to B2's after); the run stops; resume runs tasks retry --all. Harm (A1): the drain's next issues B2 beside R1, so two agents write the overlapping files at once and B2 builds before B1's remainder lands. The same root shows where a refile copies a source's after naming a refiled-away dependency (tasks:1035, the second half of i14). Caused: retry --all (work item 7) reopens such a task on every resume. Report: i13.
note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks: new refile_chain(tid, refiled) follows a task's refiles to the latest, and with_refiles(after, refiled) adds each refile in the chain of every dependency to an after list. retry_records now takes refiled (cmd_retry, its one caller, passes it) and, for each task it reopens or releases, extends its after with the refiles of its dependencies, checked through check_dependencies so a loop refuses before any write; so B2 reopened after B1 now waits on R1 too and next does not issue it beside R1. cmd_refile's default after (no --after) goes through with_refiles too, the second half of i14, so a refile no longer copies a dependency a refile replaced without waiting on its refile. USAGE (refile and retry entries) says so. Probed in a scratch run: B2 after ['t1','t3'] issued 0; refile of a task after t1 waits on t1, t3, t4.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:cmd_retry (single form). I2's refusal fires for every task retry_kind rejects that a refile replaced: 'if kind is None and t["id"] in refiled: fail("task %s was refiled as %s; retry %s" ...)', and refiles_of maps a task only to its immediate refile (tasks:1234-1235). Triggers: (1) a refiled task that closed done ('retry <it>' now advises 'retry tM' though tM is open or running, and retry tM refuses 'neither running ... nor closed as one of'); (2) a chain T -> R -> R2, where retry T names R, which is itself refused and names R2. Harm (A9): the refusal tells the operator to run a retry that is refused; before the change a done task got the accurate 'neither running ...' refusal. Caused by I2. Report: i15.
note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:cmd_retry: the refile refusal now fires only for a task that retry_kind would retry but for its refile (retry_kind(t, {}) == RETRIED), so a refiled task that closed done gets the accurate 'neither running ...' refusal again. It follows the refile chain with refile_chain to the latest refile, names the chain ('refiled as t3, then t4'), and says 'retry <latest>' only where retry_kind accepts the latest; otherwise it says what the latest stands at (new standing(): 'closed done', 'is issued and waits for an agent to claim it', 'is open and waits to be issued') and that there is nothing to retry. USAGE says the refusal names the latest refile. Probed in a scratch run for each branch.

body: .ok-planner/review/project.md, the tasks bullet: it says retry <task> on a closed task a refile replaced refuses 'task <task> was refiled as <refile>; retry <refile>', and that refile copies the source's after; after the i57/i58 fix the refusal names the latest refile, says there is nothing to retry where that refile is not retryable, a reopened task also waits on each refile of a task it waited on, and a refile without --after also waits on each refile of the source's dependencies. The review facts now describe the tracker short of what it does (A9 for a driver reading them).

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write (the reopened-task branch of the blocked_on_support loop). For a reopened, unissued test task tX it adds the holders of its own files to its waits, tests:4133 'waits |= {holders[path] for path in task.get("files") or [] if path in holders}', and discards only tX itself. holders_of maps each path to the latest open holder, so where a later open test task tY (filed after [tX] on the same test file F) or a legacy task holds F, holders[F] = tY and planned_after(tX, {..., tY}) asks tasks task set to make tX wait on tY, which waits on tX: tasks:check_dependencies fails 'task tX would wait on itself through ...' (tasks:724-726). Trigger: two scenarios in one test file, both test tasks closed blocked with support items (or tY running/partial), the run stops, and the resume runs tasks retry --all then tests tasks --stage write. Harm (A3): --stage write raises after it already filed the support tasks earlier in the filings list, and every later --stage write computes the same waits and fails the same way, so the resumed run can never pass the write stage. At base the branch ran only for closed-blocked tasks, which holders_of skips. Report: i9.
note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write: the reopened-task branch of the blocked_on_support loop no longer adds the holders of the task's own files to its waits; only the closed-blocked refile does (holders_of skips a closed task, so the refile waits on whoever holds its files now, as at base). A reopened task already holds its files and keeps its filed after list, so a later holder of the same test file (tY, which waits on tX) no longer enters tX's waits, and the tasks task set loop no longer fires. The waits.discard of the task's own id goes with it, since nothing now adds that id. As a guard for the class, new loop_refusals(filings, tasks) walks the planned waits (stored after lists, each planned file, refile with the waiters tasks refile repoints, and reopened after op) and refuses the whole --stage write, filing nothing, where any filing would wait on itself, so no half-filed stage is left; filing_text is the label after_refusals already built, shared by both. File changed: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write (blocked_on_support loop) with stage_support. Rule: decision:test-support-written-before-tests ('a support task makes the change before the test task runs again'), which the notes' resume call applies to a reopened test task. stage_support briefs an open support item only where 'path not in held' (tests:4005-4006) and its path is non-empty; the loop's skip for an unbriefed item applies only to a closed-blocked task (tests:4128 'if closed_blocked(task) and any(... not in briefed ...)'). For a reopened, unissued task T whose open item I is at a path P held by an open support task S1 that does not cite I, waits = {latest_support[P]} = {S1} and planned_after(T, {S1}); for an item with no path, waits is empty and 'elif waits:' adds nothing. Trigger: resume (tasks retry --all reopens T and S1) then tests tasks --stage write. Harm: when S1 closes (or at once, for a pathless item), close's step issues T, which runs again before any support task has made I, the reverse of the order the decision commits to; the next --stage write no longer sees T (reopened_on_support needs 'not task.get("issued")'). At base a closed-blocked task in this case waited until I was briefed. Report: i10.
note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write and stage_support: stage_write now computes blocked_on_support once before stage_support and passes the ids of the open support items each reopened, unissued test task filed (reopened). stage_support briefs such an item now even where another open support task holds its path: the new support task waits on that holder through planned_file's holders, so one writer per file holds, and latest_support[path] names the new task, which the reopened test task's planned_after then waits on. So the test task runs again only after a support task briefed with its item closes, as decision:test-support-written-before-tests says. For an item with no path, which no support task can ever brief, write_refusals now refuses the stage before anything is filed and names the command that sets the path (tasks item set <id> --field path=<support path>), in the shape of its existing change refusal. The closed-blocked branch keeps its base behavior for held paths. File changed: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write with stage_support. Work item 7's resume and the notes call 'On resume, --stage write treats a reopened, unissued test task that has an open support item as blocked on support, and adds the support task it files to that test task's after'. stage_support files no support task for an open item whose path another open support task S0 holds (tests:4005 'path not in held'), or whose path is empty; the loop skips an unbriefed item only for a closed-blocked task (tests:4128), so for the reopened task planned_after adds only latest_support[path] = S0 (tests:4132-4138), or nothing for a pathless item. Trigger: resume, retry --all, then --stage write. Harm: the reopened test task is issued when S0 closes, or at the first next, before the support it recorded exists; the outcome the notes call promises is reached only in part. Same flaw as i55 (sprint-8). Report: i12.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:main (with the sprint template's step 2, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md). Work item 7 and decision:every-stop-ends-the-goal ('a stop before the run files its first task' ends the goal through review certified printing SPRINT STOPPED). Step 2 names pre-run stops that route through step 11's 'write the stop record, then run review certified', where review certified cannot reach its stop check: (1) 'review approved refuses ... the review estate lacks the .ok-planner/review/config.json the command reads': review:main runs load_config(root) and run_under_project_python before args.run (review:2336-2339), and load_config raises 'cannot read .ok-planner/review/config.json' or 'declares no <key>' (review:152-163), so certified exits 1 before cmd_certified reaches stop_reason; (2) the tracker check 'a missing one is ... (/ok) to materialize, so stop': review loads issues at import (review:28 'issues = load_sibling("issues")') and issues loads tasks at import, so with .ok-planner/bin/tasks missing review dies with an uncaught FileNotFoundError traceback. Trigger: a /goal on a sprint in a project missing the review config or the tracker. Harm: no SPRINT STOPPED line is printed, so the /goal checker, which reads only the session, keeps pushing a stopped run: the outcome work item 7 names is reached only in part. One flaw: every pre-run stop whose precondition makes review certified unrunnable. Reports: i3, i4. Sibling in sprint-3: the documentation sprint's missing bin/docs stop (i20).
note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review: the module-level load of issues (which loads tasks) now catches FileNotFoundError only when run as a script (a sibling loader still gets the raise) and leaves issues None; main finds the root for certified by .ok-planner/ alone (project_root takes the estate marker), runs the new certified_without_config (the archived closed: check and the stop-record check, moved out of cmd_certified) before load_config, run_under_project_python, and the tracker check, then refuses a missing tracker/intake script with 'run /ok'; the owner frame catches ReviewError first and re-raises only when issues could not load. So a stop record written for a missing review config, a missing review dir, or a missing bin/tasks now yields SPRINT STOPPED exit 3 (driven in a scratch project: no tracker+no review dir, and tracker+no config, both print SPRINT STOPPED; without the record they refuse with a message). sprint-document.md step 2 already routes through step 11 and needed no change. .ok-planner/review/project.md certified facts say so. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review, .ok-planner/review/project.md

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:main. What the code does: main runs project_root(), load_config(root), and run_under_project_python before args.run (review:2333-2339), and load_config raises ReviewError on a missing or unreadable .ok-planner/review/config.json or one that declares no block_sources/standards/python/prompts_dir (review:152-163), so cmd_certified never reaches its stop check (review:2118-2120); the module also loads issues at import (review:28 'issues = load_sibling("issues")', which loads tasks), so with .ok-planner/bin/tasks missing the tool dies at import. Trigger: the sprint template's step 2 (sprint-document.md:124-129) names pre-run stops for 'the review estate lacks the .ok-planner/review/config.json the command reads' and for a missing task tracker, and stops each 'as step 11 says': write -stopped.txt, then run review certified. Harm (C4, decision every-stop-ends-the-goal, 'Every stop the executor makes before a sprint's contract holds ends the goal: a stop before the run files its first task ... At each, the session writes a stop record ... then runs review certified, which, while the record stands, prints SPRINT STOPPED'): review certified prints 'review: cannot read ...' or a traceback and exits 1, never SPRINT STOPPED, so a /goal checker keeps pushing a stopped run. Work item 7 asked for these stops and for the stop check after the config load. Reports: i26.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:planned_commit. What the code does: it matches the Window line with PLANNED_COMMIT = re.compile(r"^Planned against commit `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`\.$") (docs:100), which takes no 64-hex name. Trigger: a project whose git repository uses SHA-256 object names (git init --object-format=sha256; review:default_base, new in this sprint, names such repositories as supported). /plan-docs records git rev-parse HEAD (plan-docs/SKILL.md step 2) and the handoff rewrites the line to HEAD, both 64 hex. Path: documentation sprint step 3 -> docs:cmd_start -> held_planned_commit -> planned_commit returns None -> InputError '<sprint> holds no "Planned against commit `<sha>`." line under ## Window; plan the documentation sprint again with /plan-docs', exit 1, and the run stops. Harm (A3): no documentation sprint can start in such a repository, and the message is false, since the plan holds the line and planning again writes the same line. At the base the documentation sprint had no start check. body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp. Trigger: a documentation sprint stops midway, the owner commits a change to a file a kept ledger claim lists in its sources and the docspec's References do not cover, then a new /goal resumes with the base kept (work item 7, B27). body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:{{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}. What the code does: for a documentation sprint, once the handoff's commits are made, it writes git rev-parse HEAD into the Window's 'Planned against commit' line unconditionally (shared.md:555-559, 'write the output of git rev-parse HEAD into its Window's Planned against commit line in place of the commit the plan recorded: those commits hold only what the plan already read from the tree'). body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write (the reopened-task branch of the blocked_on_support loop). For a reopened, unissued test task tX it adds the holders of its own files to its waits, tests:4133 'waits |= {holders[path] for path in task.get("files") or [] if path in holders}', and discards only tX itself. holders_of maps each path to the latest open holder, so where a later open test task tY (filed after [tX] on the same test file F) or a legacy task holds F, holders[F] = tY and planned_after(tX, {..., tY}) asks tasks task set to make tX wait on tY, which waits on tX: tasks:check_dependencies fails 'task tX would wait on itself through ...' (tasks:724-726). Trigger: two scenarios in one test file, both test tasks closed blocked with support items (or tY running/partial), the run stops, and the resume runs tasks retry --all then tests tasks --stage write. Harm (A3): --stage write raises after it already filed the support tasks earlier in the filings list, and every later --stage write computes the same waits and fails the same way, so the resumed run can never pass the write stage. At base the branch ran only for closed-blocked tasks, which holders_of skips. Report: i9.
note: t60: stage_write now adds the holders of its own files only for a closed-blocked refile (holders_of skips closed tasks, as at base); a reopened task keeps its filed after list plus latest_support, so a later holder tY of the same test file no longer enters tX's waits. loop_refusals mirrors tasks refile's repoint of open waiters and tasks' dependency_closure, and refuses before filed_tasks writes anything; exercised in memory: reopened t1 with t2 after t1 on F gives no after filing from holders, and a forced t1-after-t2 filing is refused. plumbline clean on the file.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write (blocked_on_support loop) with stage_support. Rule: decision:test-support-written-before-tests ('a support task makes the change before the test task runs again'), which the notes' resume call applies to a reopened test task. stage_support briefs an open support item only where 'path not in held' (tests:4005-4006) and its path is non-empty; the loop's skip for an unbriefed item applies only to a closed-blocked task (tests:4128 'if closed_blocked(task) and any(... not in briefed ...)'). For a reopened, unissued task T whose open item I is at a path P held by an open support task S1 that does not cite I, waits = {latest_support[P]} = {S1} and planned_after(T, {S1}); for an item with no path, waits is empty and 'elif waits:' adds nothing. Trigger: resume (tasks retry --all reopens T and S1) then tests tasks --stage write. Harm: when S1 closes (or at once, for a pathless item), close's step issues T, which runs again before any support task has made I, the reverse of the order the decision commits to; the next --stage write no longer sees T (reopened_on_support needs 'not task.get("issued")'). At base a closed-blocked task in this case waited until I was briefed. Report: i10.
note: t60: reopened = open items of reopened unissued test tasks; stage_support now briefs such an item at a path another open support task holds, the new support task waiting on that holder via planned_file, and latest_support names it, so planned_after makes the test task wait on the support task that cites the item. Exercised in memory: t1 reopened with item i1 at P held by t3 gives support:P:2 after t3 citing i1, t1 after +0, no refusals. Closed-blocked branch unchanged. plumbline clean.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:current_section. What the code does: for each non-equal diff hunk between a live sprint's section and the carried template, it keeps the old lines unchanged where they hold no retired line ('held = sum(1 for line in old if line in retired)'; 'if equal or not held: out.extend(old); continue'). A hunk that is a pure insertion in the carried template has old == [], holds no retired line, and its carried lines are never written. Trigger: an owner trues up a project holding a live sprint laid out by v30.2.0 that stopped mid-run, then starts /goal. Evidence: running the copied current_section over the v30.2.0 template's How to execute section against the current template and retired-boilerplate.json leaves the result unequal to the carried text; missing are step 4's 'On a resumed run, file no stage twice. File no build task for a work item ...', step 6's 'On a resumed run, build the checklist from the run ...', and the test-stage paragraphs (step 3's 'Where step 2 found that the run opens its test stages, open them: ...', step 4's --stage write/verify/sweep/speed paragraph, step 7's and step 10's additions). The Completion contract comes out current. Harm (R2, B24/B26 ruling 'migrate: true-up rewrites the boilerplate from retired-boilerplate.json ... with no code change'): the migrated sprint's step 3 now runs tasks use and tasks retry --all, then step 4, lacking the resume rule, files one build task per stage again, so two build tasks write the same files; step 2 names test stages that step 3 no longer opens. Scope: the migration this sprint rules relies on current_section, and its new step 4 and step 6 lines are pure insertions. Reports: i23.
note: Walked current_section/current_boilerplate diff: stale is computed from both sections' bounds before any rewrite, sections rewritten last-first so earlier bounds hold, a pure-insertion hunk (old == []) in a stale document writes carried[j1:j2], first defaults to 0 only when old is empty. Extracted the before and after functions and ran them over the v30.2.0, v30.1.0, v30.0.0, v29.0.0 sprint and doc-sprint templates: before leaves How to execute unequal for v30.2.0, after makes both sections equal to the carried ones for every tag; a second pass changes nothing (idempotent, 0 replaced); the carried templates come out unchanged with 0 replaced, so the plan step still gates on the held count; an owner-added line is kept. Callers boilerplate_transforms and rewritten_sprint use current_boilerplate's unchanged (text, replaced) contract. ADMINISTRATION.md Live sprints line matches the behavior. plumbline lint exits 0 on both files, bash -n and py_compile pass, checks/run reports all checks passed.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:cmd_retry (single form). I2's refusal fires for every task retry_kind rejects that a refile replaced: 'if kind is None and t["id"] in refiled: fail("task %s was refiled as %s; retry %s" ...)', and refiles_of maps a task only to its immediate refile (tasks:1234-1235). Triggers: (1) a refiled task that closed done ('retry <it>' now advises 'retry tM' though tM is open or running, and retry tM refuses 'neither running ... nor closed as one of'); (2) a chain T -> R -> R2, where retry T names R, which is itself refused and names R2. Harm (A9): the refusal tells the operator to run a retry that is refused; before the change a done task got the accurate 'neither running ...' refusal. Caused by I2. Report: i15.
note: Verified t53's change to cmd_retry: the refile refusal fires only where retry_kind(t, {}) is RETRIED, follows refile_chain to the latest refile, and names 'retry <latest>' only where retry_kind accepts it. Probed in a scratch run: a refiled task that closed done gets the 'neither running ...' refusal; chain t1->t3->t4 with t4 open says 'which is open and waits to be issued; there is nothing to retry'; with t4 closed blocked says 'retry t4', which retry accepts. No caller parses the message (rg 'was refiled as'). Lint exits 0.

Trigger: B2 chained after B1 for overlapping files; B1 closes partial, step issues B2, B2 closes blocked; the session refiles B1 as R1 (B2 closed, so cmd_refile does not append R1 to B2's after); the run stops; resume runs tasks retry --all. Harm (A1): the drain's next issues B2 beside R1, so two agents write the overlapping files at once and B2 builds before B1's remainder lands. The same root shows where a refile copies a source's after naming a refiled-away dependency (tasks:1035, the second half of i14). Caused: retry --all (work item 7) reopens such a task on every resume. Report: i13.

Still wrong: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:1284-1289 retry_records adds every refile of a dependency to the reopened task's after and refuses the whole retry through check_dependencies when that refile itself waits on the reopened task. body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:{{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}. What the code does: for a documentation sprint, once the handoff's commits are made, it writes git rev-parse HEAD into the Window's 'Planned against commit' line unconditionally (shared.md:555-559, 'write the output of git rev-parse HEAD into its Window's Planned against commit line in place of the commit the plan recorded: those commits hold only what the plan already read from the tree'). Trigger: between /plan-docs step 2 (plan-docs/SKILL.md, 'Record the commit: git rev-parse HEAD') and the handoff, the owner commits a change to a file a planned docspec references, or edits such a file after the window ran so the handoff itself commits it. Harm (C1, work item 6 not reached): the rewritten line names a commit that already contains the change the plan never read; docs start (docs:cmd_start) sees planned == HEAD and passes, cmd_stamp's later_commits_bearing measures from the rewritten commit, every planned docspec is stamped at the archive commit, and the next docs window never sees the change, so the docspec can stand current, which work item 6 forbids ('A product commit made between the plan's commit and the run's start stays in the next /plan-docs window for every docspec it bears on'). The rewrite sentence is new in this change. Reports: i21.
note: Checked shared.md {{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}: HEAD is read before the first commit; the rewrite runs only where that HEAD is the commit /plan-docs recorded and git diff --name-only <window tree> HEAD -- <committed paths> is empty, else the line stands and docs start weighs the commits against the tree. Both triggers (foreign commit after step 2; edit after the window that the handoff commits) now leave the line, so docs start/stamp see the change. plan-docs SKILL.md step 2 records the tree with a private GIT_INDEX_FILE (git's index untouched); doc-sprint-document.md Window carries the tree line the handoff reads. Handoff commits only paths outside .ok-planner/. Lint clean.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:planned_commit. What the code does: it matches the Window line with PLANNED_COMMIT = re.compile(r"^Planned against commit `([0-9a-f]{7,40})`\.$") (docs:100), which takes no 64-hex name. Trigger: a project whose git repository uses SHA-256 object names (git init --object-format=sha256; review:default_base, new in this sprint, names such repositories as supported). /plan-docs records git rev-parse HEAD (plan-docs/SKILL.md step 2) and the handoff rewrites the line to HEAD, both 64 hex. Path: documentation sprint step 3 -> docs:cmd_start -> held_planned_commit -> planned_commit returns None -> InputError '<sprint> holds no "Planned against commit `<sha>`." line under ## Window; plan the documentation sprint again with /plan-docs', exit 1, and the run stops. Harm (A3): no documentation sprint can start in such a repository, and the message is false, since the plan holds the line and planning again writes the same line. At the base the documentation sprint had no start check. Same class in the same file: SHA = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$") (docs:104), which cmd_stamp uses on --commit; siblings that stood at the base and the change does not reach: review:CLOSED_STAMP (review:75), tests:SHA (tests:563), discover:823. Reports: i24.
note: Checked scripts/docs: PLANNED_COMMIT, SHA, and the new WINDOW_TREE take 7 to 64 hex; no {7,40} pattern remains in scripts/docs; cmd_start's held_planned_commit, cmd_stamp's --commit and base checks now accept SHA-256 names. Siblings in review/tests stood at the base and are untouched. Lint clean.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp. What the code does: it computes the stale ledger claims from git diff old_stamp..base only ('between = git(root, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "--relative", old_stamp, base, "--")', then stale_claims), keeps every other claim through ledger_after, and stamps a docspec not in later_commits_bearing's set at --commit. later_commits_bearing reads commits up to the parent of --commit, but only through change_reasons (docspec, references, declaring files, Where), never a claim's own 'sources'. Trigger: a documentation sprint stops midway, the owner commits a change to a file a kept ledger claim lists in its sources and the docspec's References do not cover, then a new /goal resumes with the base kept (work item 7, B27). Harm (A8, decision documentation-claim-ledger: 'the ledger never holds a claim no checker confirmed at its stamp'): the ledger keeps the claim as held at the new stamp after its source changed, and the next docs window diffs from that stamp and never marks it stale. The stale diff stood at the base, but the resume that keeps the base and puts owner commits between base and the archive commit is new in this change, so the change newly exposes it. Reports: i22.
note: The trigger still ends with the next window blind to the changed claim. With this round's i59 hunk, an owner commit after a resumed run's base that changes a kept claim's source makes the docspec bearing in later_commits_bearing, so cmd_stamp stamps it at the planned commit P (scripts/docs:894). The new stale range old_stamp..parent(--commit) (scripts/docs:888-889) then drops that claim, though it held at P, the stamp written. The next docs window diffs from P, and window_entry finds stale claims only in the ledger (scripts/docs:409-412), which no longer holds the claim; where no reference, Where, or declaring entry matches the source, the docspec reads current over a stale claim, and nothing marks the claim for a recheck. The fixer's own drive shows it: 'stamp writes 0 claims at P'. Before this hunk (old_stamp..base) the claim stayed in P's ledger and the next window counted it stale.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:bearing_docspecs (used by cmd_start and cmd_stamp through later_commits_bearing). Work item 6: 'docs window never reports such a docspec current'. bearing_docspecs unions change_reasons alone (docs:560-570: docspec file, corpus and code references, declaring files, Where paths), while window_entry also reaches a docspec on its stale claims ('entry["status"] = "reached" if reasons or stale else "current"', stale_claims checks each claim's sources, docs:311-314). Trigger: after the plan's commit, the owner commits a change to a file a planned docspec's ledger claim names in its sources and that no reference, Where, or declaring entry matches. docs start finds no bearing and exits 0; cmd_stamp drops the claim from the ledger as stale (old_stamp..base) while its text stays unchecked, and stamps at --commit since the slug is not in later['bearing']; on a resumed run an owner commit after the base is outside old_stamp..base, so the claim is kept as held. Harm: the next docs window diffs from the archive commit and reports the docspec current over a commit that made a documented claim stale. Caused (bearing_docspecs, cmd_start, later_commits_bearing are new). Report: i16.
note: The resumed-run path the defect names still ends with the docspec current. bearing_docspecs now finds the stale claim, and cmd_stamp stamps the docspec at the planned commit (scripts/docs:894), but in the same stamp the i43 hunk's stale set, old_stamp..parent(--commit) (scripts/docs:888-889), drops that claim from the ledger. The next docs window reads stale claims only from the ledger (scripts/docs:409-412), so it neither counts the claim stale nor reaches the docspec on it; with no reference, Where, or declaring entry on the source, it reports the docspec current over the commit that made the documented claim stale. The start-time path (commit before the base) now stops docs start and holds.

brief:
fix round 2; defects i43 i59
- i43: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp. What the code does: it computes the stale ledger claims from git diff old_stamp..base only ('between = git(root, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "--relative", old_stamp, base, "--")', then stale_claims), keeps every other claim through ledger_after, and stamps a docspec not in later_commits_bearing's set at --commit. later_commits_bearing reads commits up to the parent of --commit, but only through change_reasons (docspec, references, declaring files, Where), never a claim's own 'sources'. Trigger: a documentation sprint stops midway, the owner commits a change to a file a kept ledger claim lists in its sources and the docspec's References do not cover, then a new /goal resumes with the base kept (work item 7, B27). Harm (A8, decision documentation-claim-ledger: 'the ledger never holds a claim no checker confirmed at its stamp'): the ledger keeps the claim as held at the new stamp after its source changed, and the next docs window diffs from that stamp and never marks it stale. The stale diff stood at the base, but the resume that keeps the base and puts owner commits between base and the archive commit is new in this change, so the change newly exposes it. Reports: i22.
- i59: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:bearing_docspecs (used by cmd_start and cmd_stamp through later_commits_bearing). Work item 6: 'docs window never reports such a docspec current'. bearing_docspecs unions change_reasons alone (docs:560-570: docspec file, corpus and code references, declaring files, Where paths), while window_entry also reaches a docspec on its stale claims ('entry["status"] = "reached" if reasons or stale else "current"', stale_claims checks each claim's sources, docs:311-314). Trigger: after the plan's commit, the owner commits a change to a file a planned docspec's ledger claim names in its sources and that no reference, Where, or declaring entry matches. docs start finds no bearing and exits 0; cmd_stamp drops the claim from the ledger as stale (old_stamp..base) while its text stays unchecked, and stamps at --commit since the slug is not in later['bearing']; on a resumed run an owner commit after the base is outside old_stamp..base, so the claim is kept as held. Harm: the next docs window diffs from the archive commit and reports the docspec current over a commit that made a documented claim stale. Caused (bearing_docspecs, cmd_start, later_commits_bearing are new). Report: i16.

brief:
fix round 2; defects i57
- i57: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:retry_records (with ready). retry --all reopens a closed-blocked task B2 keeping its after ['B1'] (reset_task), where B1 closed partial and was refiled as R1, which is open. ready() counts any closed dependency (tasks:786-791), and retry_records un-issues only waiters whose after names a task the set reopens (tasks:1263 'named = sorted(reopened & set(t.get("after") or []))'); it never follows a reopened task's own after to the latest refile. Harm (A1): the drain's next issues B2 beside R1, so two agents write the overlapping files at once and B2 builds before B1's remainder lands. The same root shows where a refile copies a source's after naming a refiled-away dependency (tasks:1035, the second half of i14). Caused: retry --all (work item 7) reopens such a task on every resume. Report: i13.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp. What the code does: it computes the stale ledger claims from git diff old_stamp..base only ('between = git(root, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "--relative", old_stamp, base, "--")', then stale_claims), keeps every other claim through ledger_after, and stamps a docspec not in later_commits_bearing's set at --commit. later_commits_bearing reads commits up to the parent of --commit, but only through change_reasons (docspec, references, declaring files, Where), never a claim's own 'sources'. Trigger: a documentation sprint stops midway, the owner commits a change to a file a kept ledger claim lists in its sources and the docspec's References do not cover, then a new /goal resumes with the base kept (work item 7, B27). Harm (A8, decision documentation-claim-ledger: 'the ledger never holds a claim no checker confirmed at its stamp'): the ledger keeps the claim as held at the new stamp after its source changed, and the next docs window diffs from that stamp and never marks it stale. The stale diff stood at the base, but the resume that keeps the base and puts owner commits between base and the archive commit is new in this change, so the change newly exposes it. Reports: i22.
note: Walked the resumed-run trigger through cmd_stamp (scripts/docs:887-896): an owner commit after the base changing a kept claim's source makes later_commits_bearing find the docspec bearing (stale claim reason from bearing_docspecs over planned..parent(--commit)), so stale_until is the planned commit P; the stale set over old_stamp..P leaves the claim (its source changed only after P), ledger_after keeps it, the stamp is P, and the next docs window diffs from P (changed_since) and counts it stale in window_entry (docs:409-412), reaching the docspec. body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree (testing.enabled off, '- No stack:' not declared, two stories greet-drive and wave-drive), I opened a certification ledger the way /converge sprint step 1 to 4 does (tasks init converge-2026-11-08T102000, register ok-opus and ok-review, review prompt + tasks prompt register for merge fix verify restore owner-list drive drive-start sprint-review sprint-pass, tasks round start), filed the review root and closed it done with no sprint-pass task forked from it, ran tasks round start and review drives (filed t2 greet-drive and t3 wave-drive), claimed neither driver, wrote a '# Sprint certification' return block naming that ledger into the completion report, and ran .ok-planner/bin/review certified --sprint .ok-planner/sprints/certify-completion-drive.md. In the first ledger I also closed a driver 'blocked' and got the same verdict. The story promises: 'done' means the same thing for every sprint; the completion contract item 3 says 'Where the project has a story, the run's drive ran', and team-execution-cold-gate says drivers try every story and the root forks one pass task per pass. Saw: certified counts filed driver tasks as a drive that ran, though no driver was ever claimed or every driver closed blocked, and counts a review root closed done as 'the find loop ran' though it forked no pass; by contrast an open review root is refused ('holds no review task closed done, so the find loop did not run'). Evidence: 'open t2 task drive key=gate state=open issued=0' / 'open t3 task drive key=gate state=open issued=0' then 'item 3 (certification): holds: the return block names .ok-planner/review/runs/converge-2026-11-08T102000.jsonl, the find loop ran, every defect is settled, 0 stuck defects are listed, and the drive ran over 2 stories' / 'SPRINT COMPLETE: .ok-planner/sprints/certify-completion-drive.md' exit 0; and with review drive-stack printing 'unfilled' (no stack-start and no '- No stack:' line), the same ledger still gave 'the drive ran over 1 stories' and SPRINT COMPLETE, where the contract says 'drive commands unfilled or refused ... mean it did not'.
note: certified-counts-unrun-drives

body: Reviewed /plan-docs and drove its documentation sprint's steps against a scratch project (true-up of the working tree, one docspec 'usage' whose Where is docs/usage.md, a plan with one 'check' item). Followed steps 4-8 of the template exactly: checker t1 recorded one held and one false claim in docs/usage.md; per step 7 a fix writer t2 edited docs/usage.md and set the claim open; checker t3 held the rewrite and set the old claim replaced; step 8 wrote the report and ran docs complete. The story promises: a way to bring every document up to date whenever the owner chooses, so a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands, with the run going unattended to completion (decision documentation-sprints-write-the-documentation: 'the plan runs unattended to completion'). Saw: the template's own steps end in a state its own contract refuses. Step 6 runs the style pass before the fact loop and keeps it 'to the files the `write` and `change` items name', while step 7 files a fix writer 'per file holding a false claim', a `check` item's file included, and completion contract item 1 requires 'every file the run changed that still exists has a style task, except the file of a drop item'. No step files a style task for a check file a fixer changed, so the run can only finish by improvising a style task after the fact loop, whose revision then no checker reads (decision documentation-style-read-once: the style read comes 'After the writers finish'; documentation-claims-checked-until-they-hold: every claim checked until it holds). evidence: '.ok-planner/bin/docs complete --sprint .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-08-usage.md' printed 'DOCS NOT COMPLETE: .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-08-usage.md / - docspec:usage: `docs/usage.md` changed in this run and has no style task', exit 2; after a hand-filed style task t4 it printed 'DOCS COMPLETE', exit 0 (scripts/docs complete_failures: 'if kind != "drop" and path in changed and exists and key not in keys["style"]').
note: doc-sprint-fixed-check-file-has-no-style-task

body: Reviewed /plan-docs source: SKILL.md, core.md (DOC-PLANNER/WRITE/CHECK prompts), doc-sprint-document.md, and ran scripts/docs window in a scratch project (a new verb in the declaring file and a dropped exception each put the reference docspec in the window: 'declaring file changed: `cli/commands.py`', 'surface intent changed'). Divergence: the fact loop's second listing of a class's members cannot check every file. doc-sprint-document.md step 7 reads: 'File checker tasks of up to six files each, files of one docspec together' and 'The first checker task of a docspec in round 1 also lists the classes its `## Lists` names'; core.md DOC-CHECK-PROMPT has that checker 'Read the docspec ... and each file whole' (the files its brief names) and record 'each public element the documentation omits' as 'missing: <element>'. A reference docspec's layout is 'One file per class the docspec lists' (docs/shapes/reference.md), so a docspec that lists seven or more classes, or one whose reached items name only some of its files, has class files outside that one checker's brief: no checker reads them against the class listing, and the checker cannot tell whether they omit an element. The story promises: reference documentation names every element I made public. Decision surface-members-listed-at-need: 'its checker lists them again to check that the documentation misses none'; artifact-definitions SURFACE-INTENT-DEFINITION: 'its checker, to check the documentation misses no public element and lists no internal one'. Saw: only the planner's listing covers files outside the first checker task's set.
note: doc-sprint-lists-classes-in-one-checker-task

body: Reviewed /plan-docs source as above. Divergence: only the first checker task of a docspec in round 1 lists the classes (doc-sprint-document.md step 7: 'The first checker task of a docspec in round 1 also lists the classes its `## Lists` names'), and DOC-CHECK-PROMPT makes a listed element the intent keeps internal false only 'Where your brief says to list the docspec's classes'. Every other checker task of the docspec (files seven onward, at 'up to six files each') checks claims against the code alone and reads no surface intent, so an internal or gated entry a writer adds or keeps in those files passes as a held claim (the entry's claims hold against the code). The story promises: reference documentation names no element I kept internal. Artifact-definitions SURFACE-INTENT-DEFINITION: the checker lists the members 'to check the documentation misses no public element and lists no internal one'; decision documentation-claims-checked-until-they-hold has a checker that is not the writer check each claim. Saw: on a reference docspec with more than six files to check, the checker's internal-element check covers only the first task's files; the planner's and the writer's own listing are the only guard on the rest.

body: Reviewed /converge sprint step 3a.2 (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md: 'tests tasks --sprint <path> --stage speed --run <this run's ledger> --round <n> files one speed task for each of the testing.slowest slowest tests of the round that has no speed acceptance at its current test file') and the code it calls in scripts/tests: cmd_tasks passes the --run ledger to stage_speed -> speed_candidates -> speed_rows, where 'items, records = run_items(root, run, "speed"), recorded_tests(root, run)' reads speed verdicts from the certification ledger alone, and speed_settled falls back to state['acceptances'], which only 'tests stamp' writes after the archive. So a test the sprint's build-stage speed task (sprint-document.md step 4, '--stage speed --from state', recorded in the sprint's -run.jsonl) accepted at its current blob, or found product-slow, counts as unsettled in certification and gets a second speed task; a second product-slow verdict also files a second perf: entry for the same site. The verbs also disagree: 'tests slowest --sprint <path> --round <n>' reads run_file(sprint), the sprint's -run.jsonl, so it shows that test settled while '--stage speed --run <ledger>' files it. stamped_acceptances and perf_failures, by contrast, read record_runs (both runs). The story promises: the suite sped up as part of the work already run; decision tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome: 'After a failed whole-suite round ... a speed task reads the testing.slowest slowest tests of the failed round that hold no speed acceptance at their current test file' and 'A speed acceptance ... holds across sprints until the test's own file changes'. Saw (by reading, scripts/tests speed_rows ~line 4399): the build-stage acceptance is ignored inside the same sprint's certification, so readers re-read accepted tests and the batch spends its testing.slowest slots on them instead of on unread slow tests; evidence: speed_rows: 'items, records = run_items(root, run, "speed"), recorded_tests(root, run)'; cmd_slowest: 'speed_candidates(root, sprint, source, run_file(root, sprint))'; record_runs: 'return [run for run in (sibling(sprint, "-run.jsonl"), certification_ledger(root, sprint)) ...]'.
note: certification-speed-ignores-build-stage-verdicts

body: Reviewed the sprint boilerplate's archive step 4 (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md: 'tests stamp ... writes ... the speed ranking') and the next sprint's build-stage speed read (step 4: '--stage speed --from state ... the testing.slowest slowest tests in the ranking the scenario list carries'). In scripts/tests, cmd_stamp calls speed_ranking(..., testing['schedule']['form'], testing['slowest']) and speed_ranking stores 'seconds': values[-keep:], so the carried ranking keeps only the last testing.slowest seconds per test; testing.slowest is declared as 'how many of the slowest tests each run lists, and so the size of each batch a sprint's speed review reads' (ok-setup SKILL.md), not a retention count. Probe in a scratch project (stack run suite-gets-faster-over-time-7c292a1f, true-up'd, one committed test file t/test_a.py), importing .ok-planner/bin/tests and calling speed_ranking on five closed whole-suite rounds of 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 9.0 seconds at the current blob: slowest=1 -> carried 'seconds': [9.0] (median that sprint 1.0); the next sprint's --from state ranking from that carried row -> 'median': 9.0, 'cost': 9.0; slowest=10 -> carried [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 9.0]. The story promises: the suite sped up over the project's life by the work already run; decision tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome: 'The ranking orders the tests by each test's median seconds across the whole-suite rounds that ran it at its current test file's digest', and rejects 'Rank by one round's seconds: machine load in that round reorders the list'. Saw: the carried median spans only the last testing.slowest runs, so with a small batch size the next sprint ranks by one loaded round and points its speed readers at the wrong tests; evidence: 'next sprint --from state: [{... 'seconds': [9.0], 'median': 9.0, 'cost': 9.0}]'.
note: speed-ranking-keeps-batch-size-seconds

body: In a scratch git project whose .gitignore holds '.claude/' (so the vendored layer is untracked), trued up to v30.2.0 with the working tree's core, I appended a hand-written line to the stamped .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md, then ran 'true-up diagnose' and the bare 'true-up'; the story promises: the owner learns which of their files an upgrade would rewrite and can turn it down, and the decision true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps marks destructive every rewrite of 'a file a person edited, which is every file but a suite-owned file that still carries its stamp ... and holds no uncommitted or staged-only change', since only a rewrite of a file 'whose every change git holds in a commit destroys nothing git cannot restore'; saw: diagnose printed the rewrite as a plain DRIFT step, so the plan held no destructive step, the bare true-up ran with no question and no archive copy, and the hand edit is gone; the same holds in a project with no git repository. evidence: 'DRIFT: stale: .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md differs from the carried v30.2.0 rendering' / 'PLAN: 1 step(s), 0 destructive; plan 1d7ce43f24e6'; bare true-up exit 0 with 'materialized: 1 files under .ok-planner/ and .claude/ (v30.2.0)' and 'Trued up ok-planner at .../p2 (v30.2.0).'; afterwards 'grep -c "My own coding rule" .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md' printed 0 and .ok-planner/history/ held no copy. The tracked-file case works: an uncommitted edit to a tracked stamped file gave 'DESTRUCTIVE: archives a copy of .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md as it stands ...' and the bare true-up refused with 'nothing written'.
note: true-up-rewrites-untracked-edited-stamped-file

body: Review of /ok (plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md step 4) with the administration document it follows and the true-up core it calls. ADMINISTRATION.md line 47 reads: 'A stale file git does not track, every file in a project with no git repository, and every file under .ok-planner/dashboard/ or .ok-planner/.cache/ stays a DRIFT: step ... True-up writes them all', and the core does the same (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up materialize_steps: only a path in 'uncommitted(...)' gets the archive copy and the destructive mark; any other differing path gets the plain 'stale:' step). SKILL.md step 4.4 then says 'A plan with no destructive step needs no question.' The decision true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps defines destructive as a rewrite of 'every file but a suite-owned file that still carries its stamp or its fixed content and holds no uncommitted or staged-only change' and justifies the exemption only for 'a suite-owned file whose every change git holds in a commit'; the story promises the owner can turn down an upgrade once they know which of their files it would rewrite. A stamped file a person edited where git does not track it (an ignored .claude/, or no repository) is rewritten with no question and no archive copy, so the owner never gets the chance to turn it down. Driven on the core: 'DRIFT: stale: .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md differs from the carried v30.2.0 rendering' / 'PLAN: 1 step(s), 0 destructive', and the bare true-up overwrote the hand edit.
note: true-up-rewrites-untracked-edited-stamped-file
